saints.name: Saint Acacius (Agathius)
saints.feastNote: Traditional Roman Martyrology, 8 May, as Agathius the centurion. Some lists of the Holy Helpers give 7 May.
saints.about: A Roman centurion who, the Martyrology says, was denounced as a Christian by a tribune, cruelly tortured at Perinthus in Thrace and beheaded at Byzantium in the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian. His relics were later honoured at Squillace in Calabria. He is counted among the Fourteen Holy Helpers, the saints invoked together in Germany since the fourteenth century, and was asked for help against headache. Little else is known of him.
saints.patron: Invoked against headache
saints.cautions: Lists of the Holy Helpers call him Acacius or Agathius. That they meant this centurion is the usual view, but it is not certain.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/05-08.txt
Wikipedia, “Fourteen Holy Helpers” (read October 2026)

saints.name: Saint Adalbert
saints.patron: Patron of Bohemia and Poland

saints.name: Saint Agatha
saints.patron: Patron of Catania and of those who suffer from diseases of the breast

saints.name: Saint Agnes
saints.patron: Patron of young girls

collect.en: Almighty, eternal God, You Who choose the weak things of the world to confound the strong, mercifully grant that we who are celebrating the feast of blessed Agnes, Your Virgin and Martyr, may reap the benefit of her patronal intercession with You.
collect.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui infírma mundi éligis, ut fórtia quæque confúndas: concéde propítius; ut, qui beátæ Agnétis Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ sollémnia cólimus, ejus apud te patrocínia sentiámus.

saints.name: Saint Alban
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 22 June. Kept on 20 June in England.
saints.about: Britain’s first martyr. A pagan of Verulamium, the Roman town now called St Albans, he sheltered a Christian priest fleeing persecution, was converted by him, and gave himself up in the priest’s place. After a scourging he was beheaded. Saint Bede tells the story; it is first mentioned about 480. Its date is uncertain, but he has been honoured in England since the fifth century.

saints.name: Saint Albert the Great
saints.patron: Patron of natural scientists

collect.en: O God, Who made blessed Albert, Your Bishop and Doctor, eminent in the submission of human wisdom to divine faith, grant us, we beseech You, so to follow the path of his teaching that we may enjoy perfect light in heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Albértum Pontíficem tuum atque Doctórem in humána sapiéntia divínæ fídei subjiciénda magnum effecísti: da nobis, quǽsumus; ita ejus magistérii inhærére vestígiis, ut luce perfécta fruámur in cœlis.

saints.name: Saint Aloysius Gonzaga
saints.patron: Patron of young people and students

collect.en: O God, bestower of heavenly gifts, Who in the angelic youth Aloysius joined wondrous innocence of life to an equally wondrous love of penance; grant, by his merits and prayers, that we who have not followed him in his innocence may imitate him in his penance.
collect.la: Cœléstium donórum distribútor, Deus, qui in angélico júvene Aloísio miram vitæ innocéntiam pari cum pœniténtia sociásti: ejus méritis et précibus concéde; ut, innocéntem non secúti, pœniténtem imitémur.

saints.name: Saint Alphonsus Mary Liguori
saints.patron: Patron of confessors and moral theologians

collect.en: O God, Who through blessed Alphonsus Mary, Your Confessor and Bishop, fired with love for souls, enriched Your Church with a new family; we beseech You that, taught by his saving counsels and strengthened by his example, we may be enabled happily to come to You.
collect.la: Deus, qui per beátum Alfónsum Maríam Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem, animárum zelo succénsum, Ecclésiam tuam nova prole fecundásti: quǽsumus; ut, ejus salutáribus mónitis edócti et exémplis roboráti, ad te perveníre felíciter valeámus.

saints.name: Saint Ambrose
saints.patron: Patron of Milan and of beekeepers

saints.name: Saint Andrew
saints.patron: Patron of fishermen, and of Scotland, Greece and Russia

collect.en: We humbly pray Your majesty, O Lord, that, as blessed Andrew was a preacher and ruler in Your Church, so he may always intercede for us with You.
collect.la: Majestátem tuam, Dómine, supplíciter exorámus: ut, sicut Ecclésiæ tuæ beátus Andréas Apóstolus éxstitit prædicátor et rector; ita apud te sit pro nobis perpétuus intercéssor.

saints.name: Saint Andrew Kim Tae-gŏn and Paul Chŏng Ha-sang
saints.sort: Andrew Kim Tae-gŏn and Paul Chŏng Ha-sang

collect.en: O God, Who willed that through blessed Angela a new family of holy Virgins should flower in Your Church, grant us through her intercession to lead angelic lives, so that, foregoing all worldly pleasures, we may be found worthy to enjoy eternal happiness.
collect.la: Deus, qui novum per beátam Angelam sacrárum Virginum collégium in Ecclésia tua floréscere voluísti: da nobis, ejus intercessióne, angélicis móribus vívere; ut, terrénis ómnibus abdicátis, gáudiis pérfrui mereámur ætérnis.

saints.name: Saint Anne
saints.patron: Patrons of grandparents

collect.en: O God, Who in Your kindness gave blessed Anne the grace to be the mother of her who mothered Your only-begotten Son, graciously grant that we who keep her feast may be helped by her intercession with You.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátæ Annæ grátiam conférre dignatus es, ut Genetrícis unigéniti Fílii tui mater effici mererétur: concéde propítius; ut, cujus sollémnia celebrámus, ejus apud te patrocíniis adjuvémur.

saints.name: Saint Ansgar
saints.patron: Patron of Scandinavia

collect.en: O God, Who glorified blessed Anthony Mary, Your Confessor and Bishop, because of his zeal for souls, and through him established in the Church new households of men and women religious, we beseech You to grant that, with his counsels as a guide, and through the merits of his prayers, we may continually apply ourselves to seeking the salvation of souls.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Antónium Maríam Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem, apostólicis virtútibus sublimásti, et per eum novas in Ecclésia clericórum ac vírginum famílias collegísti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut, eius dirigéntibus mónitis ac suffragántibus méritis, animárum salútem quǽrere iúgiter studeámus.

saints.name: Saint Anthony of Egypt
saints.patron: Patron of domestic animals

saints.name: Saint Anthony of Padua
saints.patron: Patron of the poor and of those seeking lost things

collect.en: May the solemn feast of blessed Anthony, Your Confessor and Doctor, make Your Church rejoice, O God, so that, ever sustained by spiritual help, she may deserve to reap everlasting joy.
collect.la: Ecclésiam tuam, Deus, beáti Antónii Confessóris tui atque Doctóris sollémnitas votiva lætíficet: ut spirituálibus semper muniátur auxíliis et gáudiis pérfrui mereátur ætérnis.

collect.en: Grant us, O Lord God, to learn in the spirit of Paul the Apostle that excelling knowledge of Jesus Christ, by which St. Anthony Mary, himself wondrously learned, gathered together in Your Church new families of clerics and virgins.
collect.la: Fac nos, Dómine Deus, supereminéntem Jesu Christi sciéntiam, spíritu Pauli Apóstoli, edíscere: qua beátus Antónius María mirabíliter erudítus, novas in Ecclésia tua clericórum et vírginum famílias congregávit.

collect.en: O God, the rewarder of faithful souls, grant that we may obtain pardon through the prayers of blessed Apollinaris, Your Martyr and Bishop, whose feast we are celebrating.
collect.la: Deus, fidélium remunerátor animárum, qui hunc diem beáti Apollináris Sacerdótis tui martýrio consecrásti: tríbue nobis, quǽsumus, fámulis tuis; ut, cujus venerándam celebrámus festivitátem, précibus ejus indulgéntiam consequámur.

saints.name: Saint Apollonia
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 9 February.
saints.about: A virgin of Alexandria, perhaps a deaconess, killed in a riot against Christians just before the persecution under Decius. Her death was described by Bishop Dionysius of Alexandria in a letter preserved by Eusebius: the mob broke out her teeth and threatened to burn her unless she spoke words against her faith; asking a moment’s pause, she went into the fire of her own accord. She is invoked against toothache.
saints.patron: Invoked against toothache
saints.cautions: Her going into the fire was judged by Dionysius, and by the Church, as martyrdom, not as suicide.

saints.name: Saint Augustine
saints.patron: Patron of theologians

collect.en: Give heed to our humble prayers, almighty God, and through the intercession of blessed Augustine, Your Confessor and Bishop, kindly grant Your oft-given mercy to those upon whom You bestow great hope in Your forgiveness.
collect.la: Adésto supplicatiónibus nostris, omnípotens Deus: et, quibus fidúciam sperándæ pietátis indúlges, intercedénte beáto Augustíno Confessóre tuo atque Pontífice, consuétæ misericórdiæ tríbue benígnus efféctum.

collect.en: O God, Who graciously enlightened the English peoples with the light of the true faith by the preaching and miracles of blessed Augustine, Your Confessor and Bishop, grant, through his intercession, that the hearts of those who have strayed may return to the unity of the true faith and that we may be in harmony with Your will.
collect.la: Deus, qui Anglórum gentes, prædicatióne et miráculis beáti Augustíni Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, veræ fídei luce illustráre dignátus es: concéde; ut, ipso interveniénte, errántium corda ad veritátis tuæ rédeant unitátem, et nos in tua simus voluntáte concórdes.

saints.name: Saint Barbara
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 4 December. Left out of the General Roman Calendar in 1969; still in the Martyrology.
saints.lived: date unknown (by tradition, the 3rd or 4th century)
saints.about: A virgin martyr whose story is told in many forms. The legend says her father shut her in a tower, and when she became a Christian he handed her over to death and beheaded her himself, and was then struck by lightning. The accounts appear only centuries later, and in 1969 the Church left her feast to local calendars, judging them legendary. She remains in the Martyrology, and miners, gunners and all who face sudden danger at work still ask her prayers.
saints.patron: Patron of miners and artillerymen, and of those in danger of sudden death
saints.cautions: Her story is legend. The Church keeps her name in the Martyrology, not the details of the tale.

saints.name: Saint Barnabas the Apostle
saints.patron: Patron of Cyprus

collect.en: O God, Who gladden us by the merits and intercession of blessed Barnabas, Your Apostle, mercifully grant that we, who ask Your favors through him, may obtain them by the gift of Your grace.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos beáti Bárnabæ Apóstoli tui méritis et intercessióne lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut, qui tua per eum benefícia póscimus, dono tuæ grátiæ consequámur.

collect.en: Almighty, eternal God, Who bestowed on us the devout and holy joy of this day to celebrate the feast of Your blessed Apostle Bartholomew, grant unto Your Church, we beseech You, both to love what he believed and to preach what he taught.
collect.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui hujus diei venerándam sanctámque lætítiam in beáti Apóstoli tui Bartholomǽi festivitáte tribuísti: da Ecclésiæ tuæ, quǽsumus; et amáre quod crédidit, et prædicáre quod dócuit.

collect.en: O God, Who enlightened Your Church with the learning of blessed Bede, Your Confessor and Doctor, graciously grant that Your servants may ever be enlightened by his wisdom and helped by his merits.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam beáti Bedæ Confessóris tui atque Doctóris eruditióne claríficas: concéde propítius fámulis tuis; ejus semper ilustrári sapiéntia et méritis adjuvári.

saints.name: Saint Benedict
saints.patron: Patron of Europe

saints.name: Saint Benedict Joseph Labre
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 16 April.
saints.about: A Frenchman who tried several monasteries without finding his place there, and became instead a pilgrim beggar, walking to the great shrines of Europe and living at last in poverty in Rome, where he spent long hours before the Blessed Sacrament. The Martyrology calls him illustrious for his contempt of himself and his absolute voluntary poverty. He died in Rome in 1783, aged thirty-five.
saints.patron: Patron of the homeless

saints.name: Saint Bernadette Soubirous
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 16 April, the day of her death. Kept on 18 February in France.
saints.about: A poor girl of Lourdes who, between February and July 1858, saw a lady eighteen times in the grotto of Massabielle. The lady called herself, in the local dialect, “the Immaculate Conception”. The Church recognized the apparitions in 1862. Bernadette joined the Sisters of Charity at Nevers in 1866 and lived there quietly until she died of tuberculosis at thirty-five. Pius XI canonized her in 1933.
saints.patron: Patron of the sick and of the poor
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/04-16.txt
Wikipedia, “Bernadette Soubirous” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

collect.en: O Lord Jesus, Who bestowed on blessed Bernardine, Your Confessor, an unusual love for Your holy name, we beseech You, by his merits and intercession, graciously pour upon us the spirit of Your love.
collect.la: Dómine Jesu, qui beáto Bernardíno Confessóri tuo exímium sancti nóminis tui amórem tribuísti: ejus, quǽsumus, méritis et intercessióne, spíritum nobis tuæ dilectiónis benígnus infúnde:

saints.name: Saint Blase
saints.patron: Patron of those who suffer from illnesses of the throat

collect.en: Almighty, everlasting God, Who took up, body and soul, the Immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of Your Son, into heavenly glory, grant, we beseech You, that, always devoting ourselves to heavenly things, we may be found worthy to share in her glory.
collect.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui Immaculátam Vírginem Maríam, Fílii tui Genetrícem, córpore et ánima ad cœléstem glóriam assumpsísti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut, ad superna semper inténti, ipsíus glóriæ mereámur esse consórtes.

saints.name: Saint Boniface
saints.patron: Patron of Germany

collect.en: O God, Who, through the zeal of blessed Boniface, Your Martyr and Bishop, graciously called a multitude of people to the knowledge of Your name, mercifully grant that we who keep his feast may also enjoy his patronage.
collect.la: Deus, qui multitúdinem populórum, beáti Bonifátii Mártyris tui atque Pontíficis zelo, ad agnitiónem tui nóminis vocáre dignátus es: concéde propítius; ut, cujus sollémnia cólimus, étiam patrocínia sentiámus.

saints.name: Saint Brendan the Navigator
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 16 May. An optional memorial in Ireland.
saints.about: An Irish abbot who founded the monastery of Clonfert, in Galway, and died there in old age. He travelled by sea to other monasteries, and a famous medieval tale, the Voyage of Saint Brendan, tells of a long journey to a promised land in the western ocean. The tale is a work of imagination, but it made him the patron of sailors.
saints.patron: Patron of sailors
saints.cautions: The Voyage is legend, not history.

saints.name: Saint Bridget
saints.patron: Co-patron of Europe and patron of Sweden

saints.name: Saint Brigid of Kildare
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 1 February. A feast in Ireland.
saints.about: One of the patrons of Ireland, who founded a community of women at Kildare, the beginning of the town. Many tales of her generosity and miracles were told; the Martyrology repeats one, that the dry wood of the altar step turned green when she touched it at her veiling. Little of her life can be known for certain, but her charity and hospitality have been loved in Ireland for fifteen hundred years.
saints.patron: A patron of Ireland
saints.cautions: Much of what is told of her is legend.

collect.en: May we be aided by the intercession of St. Bruno, Your Confessor, we beseech You, O Lord; that we, who have grievously offended Your Majesty by sin, may, by his merits and prayers, obtain forgiveness for our offenses.
collect.la: Sancti Brunónis Confessóris tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, intercessiónibus adjuvémur: ut, qui majestátem tuam gráviter delinquéndo offéndimus, ejus méritis et précibus, nostrórum delictórum véniam consequámur.

saints.name: Saint Cajetan
saints.patron: Patron of the unemployed and those seeking work

collect.en: O God, Who bestowed upon St. Cajetan, Your Confessor, the grace to follow the apostolic way of life; grant us by his intercession and example ever to trust in You and to long only for the things of heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui beáto Cajetáno Confessóri tuo apostólicam vivéndi formam imitári tribuísti: da nobis, ejus intercessióne et exémplo, in te semper confídere et sola cæléstia desideráre.

collect.en: O God, Who behold how we fail in our weakness, mercifully restore us to Your love through the examples of Your Saints.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos cónspicis ex nostra infirmitáte defícere: ad amórem tuum nos misericórditer per Sanctórum tuórum exémpla restáura.

saints.name: Saint Camillus de Lellis
saints.patron: Patron of the sick, nurses and hospitals

collect.en: O God, Who endowed St. Camillus with a special gift of charity for the help of souls struggling in their final agony, pour upon us, we beseech You, by his merits, the spirit of Your love, so that in the hour of our death we may be found worthy to overcome the enemy and attain the heavenly crown.
collect.la: Deus, qui sanctum Camíllum, ad animárum in extrémo agóne luctántium subsídium, singulári caritátis prærogatíva decorásti: ejus, quǽsumus, méritis, spíritum nobis tuæ dilectiónis infúnde; ut in hora éxitus nostri hostem víncere, et ad cœléstem mereámur corónam perveníre.

saints.name: Saint Carlo Acutis
saints.feastNote: His feast is 12 October, the day of his death.
saints.about: Born in London and raised in Milan, a boy who loved the Eucharist and used his gift with computers to gather and share accounts of Eucharistic miracles from around the world. He died in Monza in October 2006, aged fifteen. His canonization, set for April 2025, was put off by the death of Pope Francis, and Pope Leo XIV canonized him on 7 September 2025, together with Pier Giorgio Frassati.
saints.patron: Often called a patron of the internet (a popular title, not an official one)
sources: Wikipedia, “Carlo Acutis” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)
Wikipedia, “Pope Leo XIV” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Saint Casimir
saints.patron: Patron of Poland and Lithuania

collect.en: O God, Who strengthened St. Casimir with the virtue of steadfastness amid the luxuries of a royal court and the allurements of the world, we beseech You, that through his intercession Your faithful may treat earthly things as naught and ever aspire to those of heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui inter regáles delícias et mundi illécebras sanctum Casimírum virtúte constántiæ roborásti: quǽsumus; ut ejus intercessióne fidéles tui terréna despíciant, et ad cœléstia semper aspírent.

saints.name: Saint Catherine Labouré
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 31 December, the day of her death. The Vincentian family keeps her on 28 November (not verified here).
saints.about: A Daughter of Charity in Paris. In 1830, as a young sister, she said that Our Lady showed her the design of a medal bearing the words “O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.” It became known as the Miraculous Medal. She spoke of it to almost no one but her confessor, and spent her life in hidden, humble service. Pius XII canonized her.
saints.cautions: The medal is a sign of prayer and trust in Our Lady, not a charm that works by itself.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/12-31.txt
The app’s own prayer o-mary-conceived-without-sin (14-sacramentals.txt), whose note dates the vision to 1830

saints.name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
saints.patron: Patron of philosophers and students

collect.en: O God, Who gave the law to Moses on Sinai's height and through your holy angels miraculously placed there the body of blessed Catherine, Your Virgin and Martyr; grant, we beseech You, that by her merits and intercession we may reach that towering eminence which is Christ.
collect.la: Deus, qui dedísti legem Móysi in summitáte montis Sínai, et in eódem loco per sanctos Angelos tuos corpus beátæ Catharínæ Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ mirabíliter collocásti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, ejus méritis et intercessióne, ad montem, qui Christus est, perveníre valeámus.

saints.name: Saint Catherine of Siena
saints.patron: Patron of Italy and co-patron of Europe

collect.en: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we which do keep the birthday of thy blessed Virgin Catherine, and do year by year renew her memorial with solemn gladness in thy presence, may likewise be conformed to the pattern of her saintly walk with thee.
collect.la: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beátæ Catharínæ Vírginis tuæ natalítia cólimus; et ánnua solemnitáte lætámur, et tantæ virtútis proficiámus exémplo.

saints.name: Saint Cecilia
saints.patron: Patron of musicians and church music

collect.en: O God, Who gladden us by the annual feast of blessed Cecilia, Your Virgin and Martyr, grant, we beseech You, that we may by virtuous conduct follow her whom we venerate in this sacred rite.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos ánnua beátæ Cæcíliæ Vírginis et Mártyris tuæ sollemnitáte lætíficas: da, ut, quam venerámur offício, étiam piæ conversatiónis sequámur exémplo.

saints.name: Saint Charles Borromeo
saints.patron: Patron of catechists, seminarians and bishops

collect.en: Safeguard Your Church, O Lord, under the continual protection of St. Charles, Your Confessor and Bishop, so that just as his concern for his flock made him glorious, so his intercession may make us ever fervent in loving You.
collect.la: Ecclésiam tuam, Dómine, sancti Caróli Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis contínua protectióne custódi: ut, sicut illum pastorális sollicitúdo gloriósum réddidit; ita nos ejus intercéssio in tuo semper fáciat amóre fervéntes.

saints.name: Saint Charles Lwanga and Companions
saints.patron: Charles Lwanga is patron of African Catholic youth

saints.name: Blessed Chiara Badano
saints.feastNote: Kept on 29 October, her birthday.
saints.about: An Italian girl from Sassello who joined the Focolare Movement at nine; its founder, Chiara Lubich, gave her the name “Luce”, light. At sixteen she learned she had bone cancer. Through two years of illness she offered her suffering to Jesus and refused morphine so that she could stay clear-minded. She died at eighteen and was beatified in Rome in 2010.
sources: Wikipedia, “Chiara Badano” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Saint Christopher
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 25 July. Left to particular calendars in 1969; he was not removed from the list of saints.
saints.about: A martyr of Lycia, in Asia Minor, who the Martyrology says was beaten with iron rods, kept safe from fire by the power of Christ, and at last shot with arrows and beheaded. Nothing more is known of him for certain. The story that he carried the Christ Child across a river comes from the thirteenth-century Golden Legend, and it made him the patron of travellers. The reform of 1969 left his feast to local calendars, but he remains a saint.
saints.patron: Patron of travellers and drivers
saints.cautions: A Saint Christopher medal is a reminder to pray and to travel with care, not a charm. The river story is legend.

saints.name: Saint Columba
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 9 June. A feast in Ireland.
saints.about: An Irish monk of royal family, called Colum Cille, born in Donegal. About 563 he settled with companions on the island of Iona, off Scotland, and founded the monastery from which he and his monks brought the faith to the northern Picts. His life was written a century later by Adomnán, one of his successors; it contains many wonders, some of them legend. He is honoured in Ireland and in Britain.

saints.name: Saints Cosmas and Damian
saints.patron: Patrons of physicians, surgeons and pharmacists

collect.en: Grant, we beseech You, almighty God, that we who celebrate the anniversary of the death of Your holy Martyrs, Cosmas and Damian, may by their intercession be delivered from all the evils that threaten us.
collect.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum Cosmæ et Damiáni natalítia cólimus, a cunctis malis imminéntibus, eórum intercessiónibus, liberémur.

saints.name: Saint Cuthbert
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 20 March, the day of his death. England keeps him on 4 September, the day his body was moved.
saints.about: A shepherd boy near Melrose, in the Scottish Borders, who saw in a vision the soul of Saint Aidan carried to heaven and became a monk. He was prior of Lindisfarne, lived for years as a hermit on the island of Farne, and was made bishop of Lindisfarne, but went back to Farne to die. Saint Bede wrote his life. He is much loved in the north of England, where his shrine is at Durham.

saints.name: Saint Cyriacus
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 8 August, with Saints Largus and Smaragdus.
saints.about: A deacon of Rome who died for Christ with his companions Largus and Smaragdus. The one firm fact is that these martyrs were buried by the road to Ostia and honoured on 8 August. Later legend says he served slaves forced to labour on the Baths of Diocletian and freed the emperor’s daughter from an evil spirit. As one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers he is invoked against temptation at the hour of death.
saints.patron: Invoked against temptation at the hour of death and against evil spirits

saints.name: Saint Cyril
saints.patron: Co-patrons of Europe

collect.en: Almighty, eternal God, Who granted to the Slavonic people that they should come to the knowledge of your name through Your blessed Confessors and Bishops, Cyril and Methodius, grant that, as we glory in their festival, we may be joined with them in fellowship.
collect.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui Slavóniæ gentes per beátos Confessóris tuos atque Pontífices Cyríllum et Methódium ad agnitiónem tui nóminis veníre tribuísti: præsta; ut, quorum festivitáte (commemoratióne) gloriámur, eórum consórtio copulémur.

collect.en: O God, Who made Cyril, Your Confessor and Bishop, an unconquerable champion of the most Blessed Virgin Mary’s divine motherhood, grant that we who believe that she is truly the Mother of God may be saved by her motherly protection.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Cyríllum Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem divínæ maternitátis beatíssimæ Vírginis Maríæ assertórem invíctum effecísti: concéde, ipso intercedénte; ut, qui vere eam Genetrícem Dei crédimus, matérna eíusdem protectióne salvémur.

collect.en: Grant us, we beseech You, almighty God, through the intercession of the blessed Bishop Cyril, so to acknowledge You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ Whom You have sent, that we may be found worthy to be forever numbered among the sheep who hear His voice.
collect.la: Da nobis, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, beáto Cyríllo Pontífice intercedénte: te solum verum Deum, et quem misísti Jesum Christum ita cognóscere; ut inter oves, quæ vocem ejus áudiunt, perpétuo connumerári mereámur.

saints.name: Saint Damien de Veuster
saints.patron: Patron of people with leprosy

saints.name: Saint David of Wales
saints.feastNote: Kept on 1 March in Wales, England and Ireland. He is not in the traditional Latin Roman Martyrology; the English Martyrology gives him on 1 March.
saints.about: A bishop and monk of the sixth century, the patron of Wales. The English Martyrology calls him Archbishop of Caerleon-upon-Usk. He is remembered as the founder of the monastery at Mynyw, now St Davids, where he and his monks lived a strict life of work and prayer. His last words to his people are said to have been, “Do the little things.”
saints.patron: Patron of Wales
sources: English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/03-01.txt

saints.name: Saint Denis
saints.patron: Patron of France and of Paris

collect.en: O God, Who on this day strengthened blessed Denis, Your Martyr and Bishop, with the power to be steadfast in his suffering, and were pleased to join with him Rusticus and Eleutherius to preach Your glory to the pagans, grant us, we beseech You, out of love for You, to despise the favors of this world and to fear not its enmity.
collect.la: Deus, qui hodiérna die beátum Dionýsium, Mártyrem tuum atque Pontíficem, virtúte constantiæ in passióne roborásti, quique illi, ad prædicándum géntibus glóriam tuam, Rústicum et Eleuthérium sociáre dignátus es: tríbue nobis, quǽsumus; eórum imitatióne, pro amóre tuo próspera mundi despícere, et nulla ejus advérsa formidáre.

saints.name: Saint Dismas, the Good Thief
saints.feastNote: The traditional Roman Martyrology commemorates the Good Thief at Jerusalem on 25 March.
saints.about: One of the two men crucified with Jesus. While the other mocked, he rebuked him, owned that they were justly punished, and asked, “Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom.” Jesus answered, “Amen I say to thee: This day thou shalt be with me in paradise” (Luke 23:39-43). The Gospel does not give his name; Dismas comes from later tradition. He is the hope of every sinner who turns to Christ, even at the last.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/03-25.txt

saints.name: Saint Dominic
saints.patron: Patron of astronomers

collect.en: O God, Who graciously enlightened Your Church by the good works and teaching of St. Dominic, Your Confessor, grant by his intercession, that she may never be deprived of temporal helps and may ever advance in spiritual growth.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam beáti Domínici Confessóris tui illumináre dignátus es méritis et doctrínis: concéde; ut ejus intercessióne temporalibus non destituátur auxíliis, et spirituálibus semper profíciat increméntis.

saints.name: Saint Dominic Savio
saints.feastNote: Kept on 6 May (formerly 9 March, the day of his death). The date in the present Roman Martyrology was not checked.
saints.about: A boy from Riva, near Chieri in Piedmont, who became a pupil of Saint John Bosco at his Oratory in Turin. Among the resolutions he made at his First Communion was “Death rather than sin”. He fell ill and died at Mondonio, near his home, in 1857, aged fourteen. Saint John Bosco wrote his life, and Pius XII beatified him in 1950 and canonized him in 1954.
saints.patron: Patron of choirboys and altar servers

saints.name: Saint Dymphna
saints.feastNote: Traditional Roman Martyrology, 15 May.
saints.about: The Martyrology tells of a daughter of an Irish king who was beheaded in Brabant by her own father because of her faith in Christ and her resolve to remain a virgin. The story is legend, and none of it can be checked. She is honoured at Geel, in Belgium, and is invoked by people who suffer in mind and by those who care for them.
saints.patron: Patron of those who suffer from mental illness
saints.cautions: Her story is legend. Prayer to her goes with good care and treatment, never in place of them; the app’s page “When it is all too much” belongs beside her.

saints.name: Saint Edmund Campion
saints.feastNote: He died on 1 December 1581, and is kept on that day in some calendars; in England he is also honoured with the Forty Martyrs on 4 May.
saints.about: A gifted Oxford scholar and tutor who became a Catholic and a Jesuit priest, and came back to Elizabethan England in secret to minister to Catholics and defend the faith. He was captured, tortured on the rack and tried for treason, and was executed at Tyburn on 1 December 1581. Leo XIII beatified him in 1886, and he was canonized in 1970 among the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales.

saints.name: Saint Edward the Confessor
saints.feastNote: Kept on 13 October, the day his body was moved (as the old Martyrology notes); he died on 5 January 1066. An optional memorial in England.
saints.about: King of England from 1042 until his death in January 1066. The Martyrology remembers him for his chastity and his gift of working miracles. He was known as a peaceable and devout king, generous to the poor, and he rebuilt the abbey of Westminster, where he is buried. He was canonized in 1161.

collect.la: Deus, qui beátum regem Eduárdum Confessórem tuum æternitátis glória coronásti: fac nos, quǽsumus; ita eum venerári in terris, ut cum eo regnáre possímus in cœlis.

saints.name: Saint Elizabeth (mother of John the Baptist)
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 5 November, with her husband Saint Zechariah.
saints.about: The wife of the priest Zechariah and kinswoman of Our Lady. Both were just before God, but childless into old age, until the angel Gabriel promised them a son, John the Baptist. When Mary came to visit her, Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and greeted her: “Blessed art thou among women and blessed is the fruit of thy womb” (Luke 1:5-45). Couples who long for a child ask her prayers.

saints.patron: Patron of Catholic schools

saints.name: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
saints.patron: Patron of the Secular Franciscan Order and of charitable works

collect.en: O merciful God, enlighten the hearts of Your faithful people, and through the glorious prayers of blessed Elizabeth, make us look upon worldly prosperity as nought, and ever rejoice in heavenly consolation.
collect.la: Tuórum corda fidélium, Deus miserátor, illústra: et, beátæ Elisabeth précibus gloriósis; fac nos próspera mundi despícere, et cœlésti semper consolatióne gaudére.

collect.en: Most merciful God, Who among other admirable gifts, endowed blessed Queen Elizabeth with the special grace of calming the tumult of war; grant by her intercession that, after the peace for which we humbly pray, we may attain everlasting happiness.
collect.la: Clementíssime Deus, qui beátam Elisabeth regínam, inter céteras egrégias dotes, béllici furóris sedándi prærogatíva decorásti: da nobis, ejus intercessióne; post mortális vitæ, quam supplíciter pétimus, pacem, ad ætérna gáudia perveníre.

collect.en: O God, Who willed to enlighten Your Church by the wondrous learning and glorious merits of the life of blessed Ephrem, Your Confessor and Doctor, we humbly pray You, that, by his pleading, You will shield her with Your lasting power against the snares of error and evil.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam beáti Ephræm Confessóris tui et Doctoris mira eruditióne et præcláris vitæ méritis illustráre voluísti: te súpplices exorámus; ut, ipso intercedénte, eam advérsus erróris et pravitátis insídias perénni tua virtúte deféndas.

saints.name: Saint Erasmus (Saint Elmo)
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 2 June. Until 1969 the Missal named him with Saints Marcellinus and Peter on this day; since then 2 June in the General Calendar is theirs alone.
saints.about: A bishop in Campania, in southern Italy, who died in the persecution under Diocletian. The Roman Martyrology says he came through terrible tortures unharmed, was kept alive to strengthen others, and at last died in peace; his body was later taken to Gaeta. The longer story of his sufferings is legend, partly mixed with that of another Erasmus. Sailors took him as their patron, and the glow seen on masts in storms is still called Saint Elmo’s fire.
saints.patron: Patron of sailors and of those with stomach pain
saints.cautions: The story that he was killed by having his bowels wound out on a windlass is a late legend, probably read from pictures that showed a sailor’s windlass as his emblem. In Spain and Portugal “San Telmo” usually means Blessed Peter González, a different man.

collect.la: Deus, qui nos ánnua beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Marcellíni, Petri atque Erásmi sollemnitáte lætíficas: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, quorum gaudémus méritis, accendámur exémplis.

saints.name: Saint Eustace
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 20 September. Left out of the General Roman Calendar in the 1969 reform; still in the Martyrology.
saints.lived: date unknown (the legend places his death about 118)
saints.about: His story is a legend. A Roman general named Placidus, out hunting, saw a stag with a cross between its antlers and became a Christian, taking the name Eustace. He lost his wealth and was parted from his wife and sons, found them again years later, and died with them for refusing to sacrifice to the gods. Scholars doubt that he existed, but the tale has long comforted people in hardship, and he is one of the Holy Helpers.
saints.patron: Patron of hunters and of those in difficulty
saints.cautions: His whole story is legend, and even his existence is doubted.

saints.name: Saint Expeditus
saints.feastNote: Named in the traditional Roman Martyrology on 19 April. Whether the present Martyrology (2004) still lists him was not checked.
saints.about: The old Roman Martyrology names him among six martyrs of Melitene, in Armenia, who were all crowned on the same day. Nothing else is known of him. His popular image, a Roman soldier crushing a crow that cries “tomorrow”, and his fame for quick answers grew in modern times. You may ask his prayers as with any martyr, but the customs around him should be treated with care.
saints.cautions: Nothing is known of his life, and he has no place in the Church’s calendar. Customs such as paying for favours, or chain prayers, do not belong to Christian prayer.

saints.name: Saint Fiacre
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 30 August.
saints.about: An Irish hermit who settled near Meaux, in France, where he founded a monastery and lived a life of prayer and hard work. Because he tilled the ground with his own hands, gardeners took him as their patron. The horse-cabs of Paris came to be called fiacres from an inn named after him.
saints.patron: Patron of gardeners

collect.en: God, Who didst vouchsafe to enkindle in blessed Fidelis the fire of thy Seraphim, and to glorify his toil to give men a true knowledge of thee by the palm-branch of martyrdom and by great signs and wonders, be entreated, we beseech thee, for his sake and by his prayers, and so establish us in the knowledge and love of thee, that we also, like him, may be found faithful even unto death in serving of thee.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Fidélem, seráphico spíritus ardóre succénsum, in veræ fídei propagatióne martýrii palma et gloriósis miráculis decoráre dignátus es: ejus, quǽsumus, méritis et intercessióne, ita nos per grátiam tuam in fide et caritáte confírma; ut in servítio tuo fidéles usque ad mortem inveníri mereámur.

saints.name: Saint Florian
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 4 May.
saints.about: A martyr of Lorch, in Austria. The Martyrology says that in the persecution under Diocletian, by order of the governor Aquilinus, he was thrown into the river Enns with a stone tied to his neck. Like many early martyrs, he is known to us only from a short account. He is much loved in Austria, Bavaria and Poland, and firefighters there take him as their patron.
saints.patron: Patron of firefighters

saints.name: Saint Frances of Rome
saints.patron: Patron of Benedictine oblates and of motorists

collect.en: O God, Who along with other gifts of Your grace honored blessed Frances, Your handmaid, with the close companionship of an angel, grant, we beseech You, that by the help of her intercession we may be made worthy to attain the companionship of angels.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátam Francíscam fámulam tuam, inter cétera grátiæ tuæ dona, familiári Angeli consuetúdine decorásti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut, intercessiónis ejus auxílio, Angelórum consórtium cónsequi mereámur.

saints.name: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
saints.patron: Patron of immigrants

saints.name: Saint Francis de Sales
saints.patron: Patron of writers and journalists

collect.en: O God, Who for the salvation of souls willed that blessed Francis, Your Confessor and Bishop, should become all things to all men, mercifully grant that we, inspired by the sweetness of Your love, guided by his teachings, and aided by his merits, may attain the joys of everlasting life.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad animárum salútem beátum Francíscum Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem ómnibus ómnia factum esse voluísti: concéde propítius; ut caritátis tuæ dulcédine perfúsi, ejus dirigéntibus mónitis ac suffragántibus méritis, ætérna gáudia consequámur.

saints.name: Saint Francis of Assisi
saints.patron: Patron of Italy and of ecology

collect.en: O God, Who by the good works of blessed Francis enriched Your Church by establishing a new religious family, grant us to imitate him by emulation of him, by looking upon the things of earth as nought and ever to rejoice in sharing Your heavenly gifts.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam, beáti Francisci méritis fœtu novæ prolis amplíficas: tríbue nobis; ex ejus imitatióne, terréna despícere et cœléstium donórum semper participatióne gaudére.

saints.name: Saint Francis of Paola
saints.patron: Patron of seafarers and of Calabria

collect.en: O God, the greatness of the humble, Who raised blessed Francis, Your Confessor, to the glory of Your Saints, grant, we beseech You, that, by his merits and our imitation of his life, we may happily attain the rewards promised to the humble.
collect.la: Deus, humílium celsitúdo, qui beátum Francíscum Confessórem Sanctórum tuórum glória sublimásti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut, ejus méritis et imitatióne, promíssa humílibus præmia felíciter consequámur.

saints.name: Saint Francis Xavier
saints.patron: Patron of the missions

collect.en: O God, You Who were pleased to gather into Your Church the peoples of the Indies by the preaching and miracles of blessed Francis, mercifully grant that we, who honor his glorious merits, may also imitate the example of his virtues.
collect.la: Deus, qui Indiárum gentes beáti Francísci prædicatióne et miráculis Ecclésiæ tuæ aggregáre voluísti: concéde propítius; ut, cujus gloriósa mérita venerámur, virtútum quoque imitémur exémpla.

saints.name: Saint Francisco Marto
saints.feastNote: Kept on 20 February with his sister Jacinta.
saints.about: A shepherd boy of Fátima, in Portugal, who with his sister Jacinta and their cousin Lúcia reported seeing an angel in 1916 and Our Lady in 1917. He loved to pray alone, to console Jesus. He died of influenza at home at ten. He was beatified in 2000 and canonized at Fátima in 2017, a hundred years after the first apparition.
sources: Wikipedia, “Francisco and Jacinta Marto” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Venerable Fulton J. Sheen
saints.feastNote: He has no feast: he is Venerable, not yet beatified, so he may be prayed to privately but not honoured in the liturgy.
saints.about: An American bishop, teacher and broadcaster whose radio and television talks, above all “Life Is Worth Living”, brought the faith to millions. He served as auxiliary bishop of New York and later as Bishop of Rochester. He was declared Venerable in 2012. A miracle was approved in 2019, but his beatification, set for that December, was postponed.
saints.cautions: Venerable, not Blessed. Check the state of his cause before release; it may have moved since this research.
sources: Not opened in this pass: the Diocese of Peoria and the Archbishop Fulton John Sheen Foundation should be checked before release.

saints.name: Saint Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows
saints.sort: Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 27 February. In the Roman Missal until 1969.
saints.about: Francesco Possenti, a lively young man of Assisi and Spoleto, who left a promising life in the world to become a Passionist, taking the name Gabriel of Our Lady of Sorrows. He died of tuberculosis as a student, at twenty-three. The Martyrology says that in a short life he gathered great merit, and that miracles followed his death. Benedict XV canonized him in 1920.
saints.patron: Patron of young people and students
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/02-27.txt
Divinum Officium, missa/Latin/Sancti/02-27.txt (his Mass in the 1962 Missal)

collect.en: O God, Who taught blessed Gabriel to meditate continually on the sorrows of Your most sweet Mother and Who, through her, exalted him by the glory of a holy life and miracles; grant us through his intercession and example so to share in the sorrows of Your Mother that her motherly protection may save us.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Gabriélem dulcíssimæ Matris tuæ dolóres assídue recólere docuísti, ac per illam sanctitátis et miraculórum glória sublimásti: da nobis, ejus intercessióne et exémplo; ita Genetrícis tuæ consociári flétibus, ut matérna ejúsdem protectióne salvémur:

collect.en: O God, Who, out of all the angels, chose the Archangel Gabriel to announce the mystery of Your incarnation, mercifully grant that we who keep his feast on earth, may have him as our patron in heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui inter céteros Angelos, ad annuntiándum incarnatiónis tuæ mystérium, Gabriélem Archángelum elegísti: concéde propítius; ut, qui festum (commemoratiónem) ejus celebrámus in terris, ipsíus patrocínium sentiámus in cœlis:

saints.name: Saint Gemma Galgani
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 11 April.
saints.about: A young woman of Lucca, in Tuscany, who lost her parents early and lived in poverty and poor health, giving herself to prayer. The Martyrology remembers her for her contemplation of the Lord’s Passion and the holiness of her life. Her confessors carefully examined the mystical experiences reported of her. She died at twenty-five, and Pius XII canonized her in 1940.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/04-11.txt

saints.name: Saint George
saints.patron: Patron of England and of soldiers

collect.en: O God, Who dost gladden us through the worthy deeds and prayers of thy blessed martyr George, mercifully grant that all they which seek thy mercy through him may effectually obtain the gift of thy grace.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos beáti Geórgii Mártyris tui méritis et intercessióne lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut, qui tua per eum benefícia póscimus, dono tuæ grátiæ consequámur.

saints.name: Saint Gerard Majella
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 16 October.
saints.about: A Redemptorist lay brother from Muro, near Naples. Trained as a tailor, he gave away what he earned to his mother, the poor and the souls in purgatory, and was called the father of the poor. He was known for obedience and for many reported wonders, and Saint Alphonsus Liguori, the founder of his congregation, said of him, “Brother Gerard is a saint.” He died at twenty-nine. Leo XIII beatified him in 1893 and Pius X canonized him in 1904.
saints.patron: Patron of mothers and of women expecting a child
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/10-16.txt

collect.en: O God, Who prepared a pleasing dwelling place for Yourself in the heart of blessed Gertrude the Virgin, by her merits and intercession, mercifully wipe away all sinful stain from our heart and grant that we may enjoy her companionship.
collect.la: Deus, qui in corde beátæ Gertrudis Vírginis jucúndam tibi mansionem præparásti: ipsíus méritis et intercessióne; cordis nostri máculas cleménter abstérge, et ejúsdem tríbue gaudére consórtio.

saints.name: Saint Gianna Beretta Molla
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 28 April (not verified here).
saints.about: An Italian doctor, wife and mother. During her fourth pregnancy a growth was found in her womb; she chose a treatment that would spare her child, and she died a week after her daughter was born. She is remembered for holiness lived in ordinary things: her work as a doctor, her marriage, her children and her faith. Saint John Paul II canonized her in 2004.
sources: Not opened in this pass: the Vatican’s canonization biography (16 May 2004) should be checked before release.

saints.name: Saint Giles
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 1 September.
saints.about: A hermit and abbot in the south of France, whose abbey, at the place now called Saint-Gilles, later took his name. Most of what is told of him is legend: a hind fed him with her milk, and when a king’s hunters shot at her, the arrow struck Giles instead and wounded him. He became the patron of people with disabilities and of beggars, and of the city of Edinburgh. He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
saints.patron: Patron of people with disabilities, of beggars and of Edinburgh
saints.cautions: His life is mostly legend.

saints.name: Saint Gregory the Great
saints.patron: Patron of musicians, singers and teachers

collect.en: O God, Who granted the rewards of everlasting happiness to the soul of Your servant Gregory, mercifully grant that we who are weighed down with the burden of our sins may be raised up by his prayers to You.
collect.la: Deus, qui ánimæ fámuli tui Gregórii ætérnæ beatitúdinis prǽmia contulísti: concéde propítius; ut, qui peccatórum nostrórum póndere prémimur, ejus apud te précibus sublevémur.

collect.en: O God, the strength of those who trust in You, Who fortified blessed Gregory, Your Confessor and Pontiff, with the virtue of firmness to protect the freedom of the Church, grant us, by his example and intercession, bravely to overcome all evil.
collect.la: Deus, in te sperántium fortitúdo, qui beátum Gregórium Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem, pro tuénda Ecclésiæ libertáte, virtúte constántiæ roborásti: da nobis, ejus exémplo et intercessióne, ómnia adversántia fórtiter superáre. saints.name: Saint Hedwig
saints.patron: Patron of Silesia

collect.en: O God, Who taught blessed Hedwig to forsake worldly vanities that she might with her whole heart humbly follow Your cross, grant that, through her merits and example, we may learn to renounce the perishable delights of the world and, by embracing Your cross, overcome all things opposed to us.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátam Hedwígem a sǽculi pompa ad húmilem tuæ Crucis sequélam toto corde transíre docuísti: concéde; ut ejus méritis et exémplo discámus peritúras mundi calcáre delícias, et in ampléxu tuæ Crucis ómnia nobis adversántia superáre:

saints.name: Saint Helena
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 18 August.
saints.about: The mother of Constantine, the first Christian emperor. She went to the Holy Land and, with her son, had the holy places cleared and churches built over them. Later tradition, first written down by Rufinus, credited her with finding the Cross of Christ in Jerusalem. The medieval English story that she was the daughter of a British prince has no historical foundation.
saints.cautions: The finding of the True Cross is told as legend, not documented history.

saints.name: Saint Henry
saints.patron: Patron of Benedictine oblates

collect.en: O God, Who on this day took St. Henry, Your Confessor, to the everlasting kingdom from the throne of an earthly empire; we humbly beseech You, that as You enabled him, protected by the abundance of Your grace, to overcome the temptations of the world, so grant that we, in emulation of him, may shun the allurements of this world and come to You with pure hearts.
collect.la: Deus, qui hodiérna die beátum Henrícum Confessórem tuum e terréni cúlmine impérii ad regnum ætérnum transtulísti: te súpplices exorámus; ut, sicut illum, grátiæ tuæ ubertáte prævéntum, illécebras sǽculi superáre fecísti, ita nos fácias, ejus imitatióne, mundi hujus blandiménta vitáre, et ad te puris méntibus perveníre.

saints.name: Saint Hilda of Whitby
saints.feastNote: Kept on 17 November in England (optional memorial).
saints.about: An Anglo-Saxon noblewoman who became abbess of the monastery of Whitby, in Yorkshire. Under her it became a place of learning, and five of its monks became bishops. In 664 a synod met there to settle the date of Easter for the English Church. The poet Caedmon took his vows under her. Saint Bede, who tells her story, says all who knew her called her mother.
sources: Catholic Encyclopedia (1907 to 1912), “St. Hilda”, newadvent.org/cathen/07350a.htm (history only)

collect.en: O God, Who in Your wondrous providence graciously send Your Angels to watch over us, grant that we who pray to You may be ever under their protection and may rejoice in their unending companionship.
collect.la: Deus, qui ineffábili providéntia sanctos Angelos tuos ad nostram custódiam míttere dignáris: largíre supplícibus tuis; et eórum semper protectióne deféndi, et ætérna societáte gaudére.

saints.name: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
saints.patron: Patron of spiritual retreats

collect.en: O God, Who, to spread abroad the greater glory of Your name through St. Ignatius, strengthened the Church militant with new power; grant that we who are struggling on earth may, by his help and after his example, be found worthy to be crowned with him in heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad majórem tui nóminis glóriam propagándam, novo per beátum Ignátium subsídio militántem Ecclésiam roborásti: concéde; ut, ejus auxílio et imitatióne certántes in terris, coronári cum ipso mereámur in cœlis.

collect.en: O God, Who enabled blessed Irenaeus, Your Martyr and Bishop, to overcome heresy with true doctrine and to establish peace happily in the Church, grant, we beseech You, that Your people may be steadfast in holy religion, and give us Your peace in our times.
collect.la: Deus, qui beáto Irenǽo Mártyri tuo atque Pontífici tribuísti, ut et veritáte doctrínæ expugnáret hǽreses, et pacem Ecclésiæ felíciter confirmáret: da, quǽsumus, plebi tuæ in sancta religióne constántiam; et pacem tuam nostris concéde tempóribus.

saints.name: Saint Isaac Jogues
saints.patron: Secondary patrons of Canada

collect.en: O God, Who, by the preaching and the blood of Your holy Martyrs, John, Isaac and their companions, consecrated the first fruits of the faith in the vast areas of North America, mercifully grant that, through their intercession, the fruitful harvest of Christians may everywhere increase day by day.
collect.la: Deus, qui primítias fídei in amplíssimis Boreális Americæ regiónibus sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum Joánnis, Isaáci eorúmque Sociórum prædicatióne et sánguine consecrásti: concéde propítius: ut, eórum intercessióne, flórida christianórum seges ubíque in dies augeátur.

saints.name: Saint Isidore the Farmer
saints.patron: Patron of farmers and of Madrid

saints.name: Saint Jacinta Marto
saints.feastNote: Kept on 20 February, the day of her death, with her brother Francisco.
saints.about: The youngest of the three children of Fátima, who with her brother Francisco and cousin Lúcia reported seeing Our Lady in 1917. She took to heart the call to pray and offer sacrifices for sinners. She died of pleurisy in a Lisbon hospital at nine. Canonized in 2017, she is the youngest saint of the Church who was not a martyr.
sources: Wikipedia, “Francisco and Jacinta Marto” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Saint James
saints.patron: Patron of Spain and of pilgrims

collect.en: Protect Your people and make them holy, O Lord, so that, guarded by the help of Your Apostle James, they may please You by their conduct and serve You with peace of mind.
collect.la: Esto, Dómine, plebi tuæ sanctificátor et custos: ut, Apóstoli tui Jacóbi muníta præsídiis, et conversatióne tibi pláceat, et secúra mente desérviat.

collect.en: O God, Who gladden us each year by the feast of Your holy Apostles Philip and James, graciously grant that, as we rejoice in their merits, we may be inspired by their example.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos ánnua Apostolórum tuórum Philíppi et Jacóbi sollemnitáte lætíficas: præsta, quǽsumus: ut, quorum gaudémus méritis, instruámur exémplis.

saints.name: Saint Januarius
saints.patron: Patron of Naples

saints.name: Saint Jerome
saints.patron: Patron of biblical scholars, translators and librarians

collect.en: O God, Who graciously gave Your Church blessed Jerome, Your Confessor and peerless teacher, to explain the Holy Scriptures, grant, we beseech You, that, with the help of his merits and by Your assistance, we may be able to put into practice what he has taught us by his life and works.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiæ tuæ in exponéndis sacris Scriptúris beátum Hierónymum, Confessórem tuum, Doctórem máximum providére dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, ejus suffragántibus méritis, quod ore simul et ópere dócuit, te adjuvánte, exercére valeámus.

saints.name: Saint Jerome Emiliani
saints.patron: Patron of orphans and abandoned children

collect.en: O God, the Father of mercies, by the merits and intercession of St. Jerome, whom You willed to be the helper and father of orphans, grant that we may faithfully guard the spirit of adoption which makes us Your sons both in name and reality.
collect.la: Deus, misericordiárum pater, per mérita et intercessiónem beáti Hieronymi, quem órphanis adjutorem et patrem esse voluísti: concéde; ut spíritum adoptiónis, quo fílii tui nominámur et sumus, fidéliter custodiámus.

saints.name: Saint Joachim
saints.patron: Patrons of grandparents

collect.en: O God, Who, in preference to Your other Saints, willed St. Joachim to be the father of Your Son’s Mother; grant, we beseech You, that we may ever enjoy the spiritual help of him whose feast we celebrate.
collect.la: Deus, qui præ ómnibus Sanctis tuis beátum Jóachim Genetrícis Fílii tui patrem esse voluísti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut, cujus festa venerámur, ejus quoque perpétuo patrocínia sentiámus.

saints.name: Saint Joan of Arc
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 30 May. A memorial in France.
saints.about: A peasant girl of Domrémy who believed she was sent by God to save France in the war with England. Called the Maid of Orléans, she led French troops, was captured and handed to her enemies, condemned by an unjust church trial at Rouen and burned at about nineteen. A second inquiry in 1456 overturned the verdict. Pius X beatified her in 1909, Benedict XV canonized her in 1920, and she is a patron of France.
saints.patron: Patron of France
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/05-30.txt

collect.en: O Lord, graciously shed light upon Your Church, so that, enlightened by the teachings of blessed John, Your Apostle and Evangelist, she may gain Your everlasting rewards.
collect.la: Ecclésiam tuam, Dómine, benígnus illústra: ut, beáti Joánnis Apóstoli tui et Evangelístæ illumináta doctrínis, ad dona pervéniat sempitérna.

saints.name: Saint John Baptist de la Salle
saints.patron: Patron of teachers

collect.en: O God, Who raised up the holy Confessor John Baptist for the Christian education of the poor and to strengthen youth in the way of truth, and through him formed a new family in the Church, graciously grant by his intercession and example that we, striving to save souls out of zeal for Your glory, may be found worthy to share his heavenly crown.
collect.la: Deus, qui, ad christiánam páuperum eruditiónem et ad juvéntam in via veritátis firmándam, sanctum Joánnem Baptístam Confessórem excitásti, et novam per eum in Ecclésia famíliam collegísti: concéde propítius; ut ejus intercessióne et exémplo, stúdio glóriæ tuæ in animárum salúte fervéntes, ejus in cœlis corónæ partícipes fíeri valeámus.

saints.name: Saint John Berchmans
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 13 August, the day of his death. The Jesuits keep him on 26 November (not verified here).
saints.about: A young Jesuit from Flanders who died in Rome while still a student, at twenty-two. The Martyrology remembers him for the innocence of his life and his faithful keeping of the rule of his order, and he is known for holiness in small daily duties. Pope Leo XIII canonized him in 1888. Altar servers have long taken him as their patron.
saints.patron: Patron of altar servers
