saints.name: Saint John Bosco
saints.patron: Patron of young people and apprentices

collect.en: O God, Who in Your Confessor, blessed John, raised up a father and teacher of youth, and willed that through him, with the help of the Virgin Mary, new religious families should bloom in the Church, grant, we beseech You, that, inflamed by the same fire of love, we may seek to win souls and to serve You alone.
collect.la: Deus, qui sanctum Joánnem Confessórem tuum adolescentium patrem et magístrum excitásti, ac per eum, auxiliatríce Vírgine María, novas in Ecclésia tua famílias floréscere voluísti: concéde, quǽsumus; ut eódem caritátis igne succénsi, ánimas quærere, tibíque soli servíre valeámus.

saints.name: Saint John Chrysostom
saints.patron: Patron of preachers

collect.en: May heavenly grace, we beseech You, O Lord, prosper Your Church, which You mercifully enlightened by the blessed virtues and teachings of glorious and blessed John Chrysostom, Your Confessor and Bishop.
collect.la: Ecclésiam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátia cœléstis amplíficet: quam beáti Joánnis Chrysóstomi Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis illustráre voluísti gloriósis méritis et doctrínis.

collect.en: Almighty, eternal God, Who to defend the honor paid to sacred images, filled blessed John with heavenly learning and wondrous strength of soul, grant that, by his intercession and example, we may imitate the virtues of those whose images we honor and may enjoy the help of their patronage.
collect.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui, ad cultum sacrárum imáginum asseréndum, beátum Joánnem cœlésti doctrína et admirábili spíritus fortitúdine imbuísti: concéde nobis ejus intercessióne et exémplo; ut, quorum cólimus imagines, virtútes imitémur et patrocínia sentiámus.

saints.name: Saint John de Brébeuf
saints.patron: Secondary patrons of Canada

collect.en: O God, Who, by the preaching and the blood of Your holy Martyrs, John, Isaac and their companions, consecrated the first fruits of the faith in the vast areas of North America, mercifully grant that, through their intercession, the fruitful harvest of Christians may everywhere increase day by day.
collect.la: Deus, qui primítias fídei in amplíssimis Boreális Americæ regiónibus sanctórum Mártyrum tuórum Joánnis, Isaáci eorúmque Sociórum prædicatióne et sánguine consecrásti: concéde propítius: ut, eórum intercessióne, flórida christianórum seges ubíque in dies augeátur.

collect.en: O God, Who wondrously enkindled St. John, Your Confessor, to promote the religious veneration of the Sacred Hearts of Jesus and Mary, and through him willed to found new religious families in the Church; grant, we beseech You, that we may honor his holy merits and may learn from the example of his virtues.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Joánnem, Confessórem tuum, ad cultum sacrórum Córdium Jesu et Maríæ rite promovéndum, mirabíliter inflammásti, et per eum novas in Ecclésia tua famílias congregáre voluísti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, cujus pia mérita venerámur, virtútum quoque instruámur exémplis.

saints.name: Saint John Fisher
saints.patron: Thomas More is patron of statesmen and politicians

saints.name: Saint John Leonardi
saints.patron: Patron of pharmacists

collect.en: O God, Who in a wondrous way graciously urged blessed John, Your Confessor, to propagate Your faith among the pagans, and through him brought together a new religious family in Your Church for the education of the faithful, grant Your servants so to profit by his teaching that we may reach everlasting rewards.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Joánnem Confessórem tuum ad fidem in géntibus propagándam mirabíliter excitáre dignátus es, ac per eum in erudiéndis fidélibus novam in Ecclésia tua famíliam congregásti: da nobis fámulis tuis; ita ejus institútis profícere, ut prǽmia consequámur ætérna.

saints.name: Saint John Mary Vianney
saints.patron: Patron of parish priests

collect.en: Almighty and merciful God, Who made St. John Mary glorious by priestly zeal and untiring fervor in prayer and penance, grant, we beseech You, that by his example and intercession, we may have strength to win for Christ the souls of our brethren and, with them, attain everlasting glory.
collect.la: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, qui sanctum Joánnem Maríam pastoráli stúdio et jugi oratiónis ac pœniténtiæ ardóre mirábilem effecísti: da, quǽsumus; ut, ejus exémplo et intercessióne, ánimas fratrum lucrári Christo, et cum eis ætérnam glóriam cónsequi valeámus.

saints.name: Saint John of Avila
saints.patron: Patron of the diocesan clergy of Spain

saints.name: Saint John of Capestrano
saints.patron: Patron of military chaplains

collect.en: O God, Who, through blessed John, made Your faithful people conquer the enemies of the cross by the power of the most holy name of Jesus, grant, we beseech You, that by his intercession we may avoid the snares of our spiritual enemies, and may be found worthy to receive from You the crown of justice.
collect.la: Deus, qui per beátum Joánnem fidéles tuos in virtúte sanctíssimi nóminis Jesu de Crucis inimícis triumpháre fecísti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, spirituálium hóstium, ejus intercessióne, superátis insídiis, corónam justítiæ a te accípere mereámur.

saints.name: Saint John of God
saints.patron: Patron of hospitals, the sick and nurses

collect.en: O God, Who caused blessed John when burning with love for You, to walk unharmed through the midst of flames, and through him enriched Your Church with a new religious family; grant that through the help of his merits, our sins may be burned away by the fire of Your love, and eternal remedies may come to us.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Joánnem, tuo amóre succénsum, inter flammas innóxium incédere fecísti, et per eum Ecclésiam tuam nova prole fœcundásti: præsta, ipsíus suffragántibus méritis; ut igne caritátis tuæ vitia nostra curéntur, et remédia nobis ætérna provéniant.

collect.en: Grant, we beseech You, almighty God, that by following the example of blessed John, Your Confessor, we may advance in a knowledge of holiness and, by showing pity for others, obtain Your forgiveness through his merits
collect.la: Da, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, sancti Joánnis Confessóris exémplo in sciéntia Sanctórum proficiéntes atque áliis misericórdiam exhibéntes; ejus méritis, indulgéntiam apud te consequámur.

collect.en: O God, Who made blessed John, Your Confessor and Teacher, an extraordinary lover of perfect self-denial and the Cross, grant that, by continually striving to imitate him, we may reach everlasting glory.
collect.la: Deus, qui sanctum Joánnem Confessórem tuum atque Doctorem perféctæ sui abnegatiónis et Crucis amatórem exímium effecísti: concéde; ut, ejus imitatióni júgiter inhæréntes, glóriam assequámur ætérnam.

collect.en: O God, Who made this a day most worthy of our celebration because of blessed John; grant Your people the grace of spiritual joys and direct the minds of all the faithful into the path of eternal salvation.
collect.la: Deus, qui præséntem diem honorábilem nobis in beáti Joánnis nativitáte fecísti: da pópulis tuis spirituálium grátiam gaudiórum; et ómnium fidélium mentes dirige in viam salútis ætérnæ.

collect.en: Arouse in Your Church, O Lord, the spirit with which blessed Josaphat, Your Martyr and Bishop, was filled when he laid down his life for his flock; so that, by his intercession, we, also moved and strengthened by the same spirit, may not fear to lay down our lives for our brethren.
collect.la: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, in Ecclésia tua Spíritum, quo replétus beátus Jósaphat Martyr et Póntifex tuus ánimam suam pro óvibus pósuit: ut, eo intercedénte, nos quoque eódem Spíritu moti ac roboráti, ánimam nostram pro frátribus pónere non vereámur.

saints.name: Saint Josemaría Escrivá
saints.feastNote: Kept on 26 June, the day of his death; not in the General Roman Calendar.
saints.about: A Spanish priest who in 1928 founded Opus Dei, to help lay people seek holiness in their ordinary work and family life. He taught that daily work, done well and offered to God, can become prayer. He died in Rome in 1975, and Saint John Paul II canonized him in 2002.
sources: Not opened in this pass: Opus Dei’s official site was refused to another agent of this project; the Vatican’s canonization biography (6 October 2002) should be checked.

saints.name: Saint Joseph
saints.patron: Patron of the Universal Church, of fathers, of workers and of a happy death

collect.en: May the merits of Your most holy Mother’s spouse help us, we beseech You, O Lord, that through his intercession we may receive what we cannot obtain by our own efforts.
collect.la: Sanctíssimæ Genetrícis tuæ Sponsi, quǽsumus, Dómine, méritis adjuvémur: ut, quod possibílitas nostra non óbtinet, ejus nobis intercessióne donétur:

saints.name: Saint Joseph Calasanz
saints.patron: Patron of Christian schools for the people

collect.en: O God, Who through St. Joseph, Your Confessor, did graciously will to provide Your Church with a new help for the training of youth in the spirit of understanding and holiness; grant, we beseech You, that, following his example and through his intercession, we may live and teach so as to acquire an everlasting reward.
collect.la: Deus, qui per sanctum Joséphum Confessórem tuum, ad erudiéndam spíritu intellegéntiæ ac pietátis juventútem, novum Ecclésiæ tuæ subsídium providére dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; nos, ejus exémplo et intercessióne, ita fácere et docére, ut præmia consequámur ætérna.

saints.name: Saint Joseph of Cupertino
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 18 September. In the Roman Missal until 1969.
saints.about: A Franciscan friar of the Conventual branch from Cupertino, in the south of Italy, slow at his studies and clumsy in work, who was known for his simplicity and for ecstasies in prayer in which he was reported to rise from the ground. Church authorities, wary of the crowds, moved him from friary to friary. He died at Osimo, and Pope Clement XIII canonized him in 1767.
saints.patron: Patron of students facing examinations and of air travellers
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/09-18.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/09-18.txt
Divinum Officium, missa/Latin/Sancti/09-18.txt (his Mass in the 1962 Missal)

collect.en: O God, Who willed that all things be drawn unto Your Son when He was raised above the earth, mercifully grant, by the merits and example of Your seraphic Confessor Joseph, that, having been raised above all earthly desires, we may be found worthy to come unto Him.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad unigénitum Fílium tuum exaltátum a terra ómnia tráhere disposuísti: pérfice propítius; ut, méritis et exémplo seráphici Confessóris tui Joséphi, supra terrénas omnes cupiditátes eleváti, ad eum perveníre mereámur:

saints.name: Saint Josephine Bakhita
saints.patron: Patron of Sudan and of victims of human trafficking

saints.name: Saint José Sánchez del Río
saints.feastNote: Kept on 10 February, the day of his death (not verified here).
saints.about: A Mexican boy who joined the Cristero fighters during the persecution of the Church in Mexico. Captured at fourteen, he was tortured and killed for refusing to give up his faith, crying “¡Viva Cristo Rey!”, long live Christ the King. Pope Francis canonized him in 2016.
sources: Not opened in this pass: the Vatican’s canonization biography (16 October 2016) should be checked before release.

saints.name: Saint Jude
saints.patron: Saint Jude is patron of desperate causes

collect.en: O God, Who have given us a way of coming to know Your name through Your blessed Apostles Simon and Jude, grant us to honor their everlasting glory by becoming more holy and to become more holy by honoring it.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos per beátos Apóstolos tuos Simónem et Judam ad agnitiónem tui nóminis veníre tribuísti: da nobis eórum glóriam sempitérnam et proficiéndo celebráre, et celebrándo profícere.

saints.name: Saint Justin Martyr
saints.patron: Patron of philosophers

collect.en: O God, Who through the preaching of the Cross, which is to them that perish foolishness, didst wonderfully teach unto thy blessed martyr Justin the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus Our Lord, grant unto us at his prayers the grace to cast off all false teaching and ever to hold fast to the faith.
collect.la: Deus, qui per stultítiam Crucis eminéntem Jesu Christi sciéntiam beátum Justínum Mártyrem mirabíliter docuísti: ejus nobis intercessióne concéde; ut, errórum circumventióne depúlsa, fídei firmitátem consequámur.

saints.name: Saint Kateri Tekakwitha
saints.patron: Patron of ecology and of the indigenous peoples of North America

saints.name: Saint Lawrence
saints.patron: Patron of deacons, cooks and the poor

collect.en: Grant us, we beseech You, almighty God, to extinguish the flames of our sins, as You granted St. Lawrence to overcome the fires of his tortures.
collect.la: Da nobis, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: vitiórum nostrorum flammas exstínguere; qui beáto Lauréntio tribuísti tormentórum suórum incéndia superáre.

collect.en: O God, Who, to enable him to accomplish tasks, no matter how difficult, for the glory of Your name and the salvation of souls, endowed blessed Lawrence, Your Confessor and Doctor, with the spirit of wisdom and fortitude; grant us, in the same spirit, ever to know our duty, and through his prayers to do it.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad árdua quæque pro nóminis tui glória et animárum salúte beáto Lauréntio, Confessóri tuo atque Doctóri, spíritum sapiéntiæ et fortitúdinis contulísti: da nobis in eódem spíritu et agénda cognóscere; et cógnita, ejus intercessióne, perfícere.

saints.name: Saint Lazarus
saints.patron: Saint Martha is patron of cooks and of those who serve in the home

saints.name: Saint Louis
saints.patron: Patron of the Secular Franciscan Order

collect.en: O God, Who transported Your blessed Confessor Louis from an earthly throne to the glory of the heavenly kingdom, by his merits and intercession we beseech You to make us of the company of the King of kings, Jesus Christ Your Son.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Ludovícum Confessórem tuum de terréno regno ad cœléstis regni glóriam transtulísti: ejus, quǽsumus, méritis et intercessióne; Regis regum Jesu Christi, Fílii tui, fácias nos esse consórtes:

saints.name: Saint Louis Martin
saints.feastNote: Kept on 12 July with his wife, Saint Zélie (their wedding was on 13 July 1858).
saints.about: A watchmaker and jeweller of Alençon, in Normandy, who married Zélie Guérin in 1858. Of their nine children, five daughters lived to grow up; the youngest was Saint Thérèse of Lisieux. He later gave up his own trade to help with Zélie’s lace business. In his last years he suffered strokes and a long illness of mind, and spent three years in a hospital at Caen. He and Zélie were canonized together in 2015.
sources: Wikipedia, “Louis Martin and Marie-Azélie Guérin” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)
Wikipedia, “Thérèse of Lisieux” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Saint Louise de Marillac
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 15 March.
saints.about: A widow of Paris who, with Saint Vincent de Paul, founded the Daughters of Charity, a community of women given to the service of the poor and the sick. The Martyrology remembers her as wholly given to relieving the needy. She was canonized by Pius XI.
saints.patron: Patron of social workers
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/03-15.txt
Catholic Encyclopedia (1907 to 1912), “Venerable Louise de Marillac Le Gras”, newadvent.org/cathen/09133b.htm (index entry only; the article was not opened) (history only)

saints.name: Saint Lucy of Syracuse
saints.patron: Patron of the blind and of those with eye disease

saints.name: Saint Luke
saints.patron: Patron of physicians and artists

collect.en: O Lord, we beseech You, that Luke, Your holy Evangelist, who for the honor of Your name bore continually in his body the suffering of the cross, may intercede in our behalf.
collect.la: Intervéniat pro nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, sanctus tuus Lucas Evangélista: qui crucis mortificatiónem júgiter in suo córpore, pro tui nóminis honóre, portávit.

collect.en: O God, Who gladden us each year by the feast of Your holy Martyrs, Marcellinus, Peter and Erasmus, graciously grant that, as we rejoice in their merits, we may be inspired by their example.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos ánnua beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Marcellíni, Petri atque Erásmi sollemnitáte lætíficas: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, quorum gaudémus méritis, accendámur exémplis.

saints.name: Saint Margaret Clitherow
saints.feastNote: Kept on 30 August in England with Saints Anne Line and Margaret Ward. She died on 25 March 1586.
saints.about: The wife of a butcher of York, called the Pearl of York. After becoming a Catholic she hid priests in her house and arranged Masses in secret. Arrested in 1586, she refused to plead, so that her children and servants would not be made to give evidence against her, and was pressed to death under a weighted door. She was canonized in 1970 among the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales.
sources: Catholic Encyclopedia (1907 to 1912), “Ven. Margaret Clitherow”, newadvent.org/cathen/04059b.htm (history only)
Wikipedia, “National calendars of the Roman Rite” (England, 30 August)

collect.en: O Lord Jesus Christ, Who wondrously revealed the unsearchable riches of Your Heart to blessed Margaret Mary, the Virgin, grant us, by her merits and through imitating her, to love You in all things and above all things, so that we may be found worthy to possess a lasting dwelling place in Your Heart itself.
collect.la: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui investigábiles divítias Cordis tui beátæ Margarítæ Maríæ Vírgini mirabíliter revelásti: da nobis ejus méritis et imitatióne; ut, te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, jugem in eódem Corde tuo mansiónem habére mereámur:

saints.name: Saint Margaret of Antioch
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 20 July. Left out of the General Roman Calendar in 1969; still in the Martyrology.
saints.about: A virgin martyr of Antioch in Pisidia, in Asia Minor; even the century in which she lived is uncertain. Her legend, much loved in the Middle Ages, says she was swallowed by the devil in the form of a dragon and came out unharmed by the power of the cross. Because of this escape, women about to give birth asked her prayers, and she is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
saints.patron: Patron of expectant mothers
saints.cautions: Her story is legend.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/07-20.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/07-20.txt
Wikipedia, “Margaret the Virgin” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)
Wikipedia, “Fourteen Holy Helpers” (read October 2026)

saints.name: Saint Margaret of Scotland
saints.patron: Patron of Scotland

collect.en: O God, Who made blessed Queen Margaret glorious by her remarkable charity toward the poor; grant, by her intercession and example, that Your charity may continually increase in our hearts.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátam Margarítam regínam exímia in páuperes caritáte mirábilem effecísti: da; ut, ejus intercessióne et exémplo, tua in córdibus nostris cáritas júgiter augeátur.

saints.name: Saint Maria Goretti
saints.patron: Patron of young people

saints.name: Saint Mark the Evangelist
saints.patron: Patron of Venice

collect.en: O God, Who didst exalt thy blessed Evangelist Mark, by giving him grace to preach thine Evangel, grant unto us, we beseech thee, ever to follow more and more what he teacheth, and ever to be shielded from all evil by his prayers.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Marcum Evangelístam tuum evangélicæ prædicatiónis grátia sublimásti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ejus nos semper et eruditióne profícere et oratióne deféndi.

saints.name: Saint Martha
saints.patron: Saint Martha is patron of cooks and of those who serve in the home

saints.name: Saint Martin de Porres
saints.patron: Patron of social justice and of people of mixed race

saints.name: Saint Martin of Tours
saints.patron: Patron of soldiers

collect.en: O God, Who see that we cannot survive by any power of our own, mercifully grant that, by the intercession of blessed Martin, Your Confessor and Bishop, we may be made safe from all harm.
collect.la: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra virtúte subsístimus: concéde propítius; ut, intercessióne beáti Martíni Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, contra ómnia advérsa muniámur.

saints.name: Saint Mary MacKillop
saints.feastNote: Kept on 8 August; a solemnity in Australia.
saints.about: Australia’s first canonized saint. With Father Julian Tenison Woods she founded the Sisters of Saint Joseph of the Sacred Heart, who opened schools and homes for poor children in the outback and the cities. For a short time in 1871 she was wrongly excommunicated, and was soon restored. She was canonized in 2010.
sources: Wikipedia, “List of saints from Oceania” (founder of the Sisters of St Joseph of the Sacred Heart; canonized 2010)
Wikipedia, “National calendars of the Roman Rite” (Australia, 8 August, solemnity)

collect.en: May the prayers of blessed Mary Magdalen help us, O Lord, Who were moved by her prayers and brought back alive from the grave her brother Lazarus, dead for four days.
collect.la: Beátæ Maríæ Magdalénæ, quǽsumus, Dómine, suffrágiis adjuvémur: cujus précibus exorátus, quatriduánum fratrem Lázarum vivum ab ínferis resuscitásti:

collect.en: O God, lover of chastity, Who endowed with heavenly gifts blessed Mary Magdalen, a virgin on fire with love for You, grant that we who keep this feast-day in her honor may imitate her by purity and love.
collect.la: Deus, virginitátis amátor, qui beátam Maríam Magdalénam Vírginem, tuo amóre succénsam, cœléstibus donis decorásti: da; ut, quam festíva celebritáte venerámur, puritáte et caritáte imitémur.

saints.name: Saint Mary of Bethany
saints.patron: Saint Martha is patron of cooks and of those who serve in the home

saints.name: Saint Matthew
saints.patron: Patron of bankers, accountants and tax collectors

collect.en: May we be helped, O Lord, by the prayers of the blessed Apostle and Evangelist Matthew, that what we ourselves cannot obtain, may be granted by his intercession.
collect.la: Beáti Apóstoli et Evangelístæ Matthǽi, Dómine, précibus adjuvémur: ut, quod possibílitas nostra non óbtinet, ejus nobis intercessióne donétur.

collect.en: O God, Who didst choose thy blessed servant Matthias to be of the number of the twelve Apostles, grant, we beseech thee, that thy Church, being upholden by his prayers, may ever feel about her the arms of thy most mighty protection.
collect.la: Déus, qui beátum Matthíam Apostolórum tuórum collégio sociásti: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut, eius interventióne, tuæ circa nos pietátis sémper víscera sentiámus.

saints.name: Saint Methodius
saints.patron: Co-patrons of Europe

collect.en: Almighty, eternal God, Who granted to the Slavonic people that they should come to the knowledge of your name through Your blessed Confessors and Bishops, Cyril and Methodius, grant that, as we glory in their festival, we may be joined with them in fellowship.
collect.la: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui Slavóniæ gentes per beátos Confessóris tuos atque Pontífices Cyríllum et Methódium ad agnitiónem tui nóminis veníre tribuísti: præsta; ut, quorum festivitáte (commemoratióne) gloriámur, eórum consórtio copulémur.

collect.en: O God, Who assign according to a wondrous order the duties of Angels and men, mercifully grant that our life on earth be guarded by those who continually stand in Your presence and minister to You in heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui, miro ordine, Angelórum ministéria hominúmque dispénsas: concéde propítius; ut, a quibus tibi ministrántibus in cœlo semper assístitur, ab his in terra vita nostra muniátur.

saints.name: Saint Monica
saints.patron: Patron of mothers

collect.en: May the holy feast of Your Martyrs, Nereus, Achilleus, Domitilla and Pancras, ever comfort us, we beseech You, O Lord, and make us worthy to serve You.
collect.la: Semper nos, Dómine, Mártyrum tuórum Nérei, Achíllei, Domitíllæ atque Pancrátii fóveat, quǽsumus, beáta solémnitas: et tuo dignos reddat obséquio.

saints.name: Saint Nicholas
saints.patron: Patron of children and sailors

collect.en: O God, You who made the holy Bishop Nicholas renowned for countless miracles, grant, we beseech You, that by his merits and prayers we may be saved from the fires of hell.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Nicoláum Pontíficem innúmeris decorásti miráculis: tríbue, quǽsumus; ut ejus méritis et précibus a gehénnæ incéndiis liberémur.

saints.name: Saint Nicholas of Tolentino
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 10 September. In the Roman Missal until 1969.
saints.about: A friar of the Hermits of Saint Augustine who spent most of his life at Tolentino, in central Italy, as a preacher, confessor and friend of the poor and the sick. He prayed much for the souls in purgatory, and Catholics have long asked his prayers for the dead.
saints.patron: Patron of the holy souls in purgatory
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/09-10.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/09-10.txt
Catholic Encyclopedia index: “Nicholas of Tolentino, Saint” (newadvent.org/cathen/11065a.htm, which gives his death as 1306; the article could not be opened)

collect.en: O God, Who made blessed Norbert, Your Confessor and Bishop, a brilliant preacher of Your word, and through him enriched Your Church with a new religious family, grant, we beseech You, that by his prayerful intercession and Your help, we may be able to do what he has taught us by his words and deeds.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Norbértum Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem verbi tui præcónem exímium effecísti, et per eum Ecclésiam tuam nova prole fœcundásti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, ejúsdem suffragántibus méritis, quod ore simul et ópere dócuit, te adjuvánte, exercére valeámus.

saints.name: Saint Oliver Plunkett
saints.feastNote: Kept on 1 July, a memorial in Ireland and an optional memorial in England.
saints.about: Archbishop of Armagh and Primate of All Ireland, who worked for his people through years of persecution, often in hiding. Falsely accused of a plot against the king, he was tried in London and hanged, drawn and quartered at Tyburn on 1 July 1681, the last Catholic martyr to die there. He was canonized in 1975.
sources: Wikipedia, “National calendars of the Roman Rite” (Ireland and England, 1 July)
Catholic Encyclopedia index: “Plunket, Blessed Oliver” (newadvent.org/cathen/12169b.htm; the article could not be opened)

saints.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
saints.patron: Patroness of the Americas

collect.en: O God, Who willed that, under the special patronage of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we be laden with perpetual favors, grant to Your suppliants that, as we this day rejoice in her commemoration on earth, we may enjoy the vision of her in heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui sub beatíssimæ Vírginis Maríæ singulári patrocínio constitútos perpétuis benefíciis nos cumulári voluísti: præsta supplícibus tuis; ut, cujus hódie commemoratióne lætámur in terris, ejus conspéctu perfruámur in cælis.

collect.en: O God, who by the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin prepared a worthy dwelling for Your Son, we humbly beseech You that, recalling the apparition of the same Virgin, we may obtain health for both soul and body.
collect.la: Deus, qui per immaculátam Vírginis Conceptiónem dignum Filio tuo habitáculum præparásti: súpplices a te quǽsumus; ut, ejúsdem Vírginis Apparitiónem celebrántes, salútem mentis et córporis consequámur.

collect.en: O God, Who honored the Order of Carmel with the special title of the most blessed Mary, ever Virgin, Your mother, graciously grant, that we who this day honor her commemoration with solemn rites, defended by her care, may be found worthy to attain everlasting happiness.
collect.la: Deus, qui beatíssimæ semper Vírginis et Genetrícis tuæ Maríæ singulári título Carméli órdinem decorásti: concéde propítius; ut, cujus hódie Commemoratiónem sollémni celebrámus offício, ejus muníti præsídiis, ad gáudia sempitérna perveníre mereámur:

collect.en: O God, Whose only-begotten Son, by His life, death and resurrection, has merited for us the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we beseech You, that, meditating on those mysteries in the most holy Rosary of the Blessed Virgin Mary, we may imitate what they contain and obtain what they promise.
collect.la: Deus, cujus Unigénitus per vitam, mortem et resurrectiónem suam nobis salútis ætérnæ præmia comparávit: concéde, quǽsumus; ut, hæc mystéria sacratíssimo beátæ Maríæ Vírginis Rosário recoléntes, et imitémur, quod cóntinent, et quod promíttunt, assequámur.

saints.name: Saint Pantaleon
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 27 July.
saints.about: A physician of Nicomedia, in Asia Minor, brought to the faith by a priest named Hermolaus, who was put to death for Christ under the emperor Maximian. Christians were honouring him by the fifth century, so his martyrdom is well attested, but the later account of his many tortures is legend. Doctors and midwives take him as their patron, and he is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.
saints.patron: Patron of physicians and midwives
saints.cautions: The tales of his tortures, and of a relic of his blood said to turn liquid, are not history.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/07-27.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/07-27.txt
Wikipedia, “Saint Pantaleon” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)
Wikipedia, “Fourteen Holy Helpers” (read October 2026)

saints.name: Saint Patrick
saints.patron: Patron of Ireland

collect.en: O God, Who graciously sent blessed Patrick, Your Confessor and Bishop, to preach Your glory to the nations, grant through his merits and intercession, that by Your mercy we may be able to accomplish what You command.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad prædicándam géntibus glóriam tuam beátum Patrícium Confessórem atque Pontíficem míttere dignátus es: ejus méritis et intercessióne concéde; ut, quæ nobis agénda prǽcipis, te miseránte adimplére possímus.

saints.name: Saint Paul
saints.patron: Patrons of the city of Rome

collect.en: O God, Who made this day holy by the martyrdom of Your Apostles Peter and Paul, grant Your Church to follow in all things the teaching of those from whom she first received the faith.
collect.la: Deus, qui hodiérnam diem Apostolórum tuórum Petri et Pauli martýrio consecrásti: da Ecclésiæ tuæ, eórum in ómnibus sequi præcéptum; per quos religiónis sumpsit exórdium.

collect.en: Lord Jesus Christ, Who didst gift thine holy servant Paul with great love that he might preach the mystery of thy cross, and hast been pleased that through him a new family should grow up in thy Church, grant unto us at his prayers that upon earth we may so call thy sufferings to mind as worthily to gain the fruit thereof in heaven.
collect.la: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui, ad mystérium Crucis prædicándum, sanctum Paulum singulári caritáte donásti, et per eum novam in Ecclésia famíliam floréscere voluísti: ipsíus nobis intercessióne concéde; ut, passiónem tuam júgiter recoléntes in terris, ejúsdem fructum cónsequi mereámur in cœlis:

collect.en: O God, Who promised to those who forsake all things in this world for You a hundred-fold reward in the world to come and life everlasting, mercifully grant that, following closely in the footsteps of the holy Bishop Paulinus, we may look upon earthly things as nought, and long only for those of heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui ómnia pro te in hoc sǽculo relinquéntibus, céntuplum in futúro et vitam ætérnam promisísti: concéde propítius; ut, sancti Pontíficis Paulíni vestígiis inhæréntes, valeámus terréna despícere et sola cœléstia desideráre:

saints.name: Saint Peregrine Laziosi
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 1 May, the day of his death. The Servite Order may keep him on another day (often given as 4 May; not verified).
saints.about: A friar of the Servants of Mary at Forlì, in northern Italy. The story told of him is that he suffered from a wound in his leg that was to be cut off, prayed through the night before a crucifix, and was found healed in the morning. He died on 1 May 1345 and was canonized in 1726. People with cancer, and those who care for them, have long asked his prayers.
saints.patron: Patron of those with cancer
saints.cautions: Pray to him alongside medical care, never instead of it.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/05-01.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/05-01.txt

Findings of the novenas research in this project (novenas.md), which opened Wikipedia, “Peregrine Laziosi” (death 1 May 1345; canonized by Benedict XIII, 27 December 1726; the healing given as tradition)

saints.name: Saint Peter
saints.patron: Patrons of the city of Rome

collect.en: O God, Who made this day holy by the martyrdom of Your Apostles Peter and Paul, grant Your Church to follow in all things the teaching of those from whom she first received the faith.
collect.la: Deus, qui hodiérnam diem Apostolórum tuórum Petri et Pauli martýrio consecrásti: da Ecclésiæ tuæ, eórum in ómnibus sequi præcéptum; per quos religiónis sumpsit exórdium.

collect.en: O God, who didst give strength and learning to blessed Peter thy Confessor for the defense of the Catholic faith, mercifully grant, that by his example and teaching the erring may be saved and the faithful remain constant in the confession of truth.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad tuéndam cathólicam fidem beátum Petrum Confessórem tuum virtúte et doctrína roborásti: concéde propítius; ut ejus exémplis et mónitis errántes ad salútem resipíscant, et fidéles in veritátis confessióne persevérent.

saints.name: Saint Peter Chanel
saints.patron: Patron of Oceania

collect.en: O God, Who willed to foreshow divinely that blessed Peter Chrysologus would be a great Doctor to rule and teach Your Church, grant, we beseech You, that we may be worthy to have him as our intercessor in heaven who on earth was a teacher of life.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Petrum Chrysólogum Doctórem egrégium, divínitus præmonstrátum, ad regéndam et instruéndam Ecclésiam tuam éligi voluísti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, quem Doctórem vitæ habúimus in terris, intercessórem habére mereámur in cœlis.

saints.name: Saint Peter Claver
saints.patron: Patron of missions to African peoples

collect.en: Grant us, we beseech You, almighty God, to follow the counsel and examples of St. Peter, Your Confessor and Bishop, so that by setting earthly goods at naught we may attain everlasting happiness.
collect.la: Concéde nos, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: beáti Petri Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis mónita et exémpla sectári; ut per terréstrium rerum contémptum ætérna gáudia consequámur.

saints.name: Blessed Peter González (San Telmo)
saints.feastNote: Kept on 14 April in the Dominican calendar. He is not in the General Roman Calendar.
saints.about: A Dominican friar of Galicia, in north-west Spain. Sailors of Spain and Portugal took him as their patron and call him San Telmo, a name that came to him by confusion with Saint Erasmus, whom English speakers call Saint Elmo. Pope Innocent IV beatified him in 1254, and Benedict XIV confirmed the honour paid to him in 1741. He is a Blessed, not a canonized saint.
saints.patron: Patron of Spanish and Portuguese sailors
sources: Wikipedia, “Erasmus of Formiae” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

collect.en: O God, Who gladden us each year by the feast of Your holy Apostles Philip and James, graciously grant that, as we rejoice in their merits, we may be inspired by their example.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos ánnua Apostolórum tuórum Philíppi et Jacóbi sollemnitáte lætíficas: præsta, quǽsumus: ut, quorum gaudémus méritis, instruámur exémplis.

saints.name: Saint Philip Neri
saints.patron: A patron of Rome

collect.en: O God, Who raised blessed Philip, Your Confessor, to the glory of Your Saints, graciously grant that we who rejoice in his feast may profit by the example of his virtues.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Philíppum Confessórem tuum Sanctórum tuórum glória sublimásti: concéde propítius; ut, cujus sollemnitáte lætámur, ejus virtútum proficiámus exémplo.

saints.name: Saint Philomena
saints.feastNote: Her feast (formerly 11 August, in some places) was removed from all calendars in 1961.
saints.about: Devotion to Saint Philomena grew in the nineteenth century around remains found in a Roman catacomb in 1802, and Saint John Vianney loved her. In 1961 the Church removed her feast from all calendars, because nothing certain is known of her. The app keeps to saints whose memory the Church celebrates, but a reader may still ask her prayers in private.
saints.cautions: Nothing certain is known of her. Her liturgical feast was removed in 1961. The phrase “cult suppressed” here means her public liturgical honour, not private prayer; whether private devotion is formally permitted was not verified.

saints.name: Saint Pier Giorgio Frassati
saints.feastNote: His feast is 4 July, the day of his death.
saints.about: A young man of a well-to-do family in Turin who gave his time and his money to the poor of the city. He loved mountain climbing, and his motto, “verso l’alto”, means “toward the heights”. He joined the Third Order of Saint Dominic in 1922. He died of polio in 1925, aged twenty-four. Saint John Paul II beatified him in 1990, and Pope Leo XIV canonized him on 7 September 2025, together with Carlo Acutis.
saints.patron: Patron of young people, students and mountaineers
sources: Wikipedia, “Pier Giorgio Frassati” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)
Wikipedia, “Pope Leo XIV” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

collect.en: O, God, Who graciously chose blessed Pius as Supreme Pontiff, to crush the enemies of Your Church and to restore divine worship, grant that we may be guarded by his help and remain so steadfast in Your service that, having overcome the snares of all enemies, we may enjoy a lasting peace.
collect.la: Deus, qui, ad conteréndos Ecclésiæ tuæ hostes et ad divínum cultum reparándum, beátum Pium Pontíficem Máximum elígere dignátus es: fac nos ipsíus deféndi præsídiis et ita tuis inhærére obséquiis; ut, ómnium hóstium superátis insídiis, perpétua pace lætémur. [Secreta] (nisi rubrica 196) [Postcommunio] (nisi rubrica 196)

collect.en: O God Who, for the defense of the Catholic faith and the restoration of all things in Christ, filled St. Pius, the Supreme Pontiff, with heavenly wisdom and apostolic fearlessness, mercifully grant that, by following his teachings and examples, we may receive Your eternal rewards.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad tuéndam cathólicam fidem, et univérsa in Christo instauránda sanctum Pium, Summum Pontíficem, cælésti sapiéntia et apostólica fortitúdine replevísti: concéde propítius; ut, ejus institúta et exémpla sectántes, præmia consequámur ætérna.

collect.en: O God, Who gave blessed Raphael the Archangel as a traveling companion to Your servant Tobias, grant us, Your servants, ever to be protected by his guardianship and by his help.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Raphaélem Archángelum Tobíæ fámulo tuo cómitem dedísti in via: concéde nobis fámulis tuis; ut ejúsdem semper protegámur custódia et muniámur auxílio.

saints.name: Saint Raymond Nonnatus
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 31 August. In the Roman Missal until 1969.
saints.about: A Catalan friar of the Mercedarian Order, which ransomed Christians held captive in North Africa. His name, “not born”, recalls that he was delivered from his mother’s womb after she had died. In Algiers he gave himself as a hostage for captives and, the story says, had his lips padlocked to stop him preaching. He was later made a cardinal and died at Cardona in 1240. Women in labour and the falsely accused ask his prayers.
saints.patron: Patron of women in childbirth and of midwives
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/08-31.txt

collect.en: O God, Who made blessed Raymund, Your Confessor, famous for delivering Your faithful from the captivity of the infidels, grant us by his intercession that, having been released from the bonds of our sins, we may with free minds do what is pleasing to You.
collect.la: Deus, qui in liberándis fidélibus tuis ab impiórum captivitáte beátum Raymúndum Confessórem tuum mirábilem effecísti: ejus nobis intercessióne concéde; ut, a peccatórum vínculis absolúti, quæ tibi sunt plácita, líberis méntibus exsequámur.

saints.name: Saint Raymond of Penyafort
saints.patron: Patron of canon lawyers

collect.en: O God, You Who chose blessed Raymond to be a renowned minister of the sacrament of Penance, and miraculously brought him through the waves of the sea, grant that by his intercession we may produce good results from our penitence and reach the haven of eternal salvation.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Raymúndum pœniténtiæ sacraménti insígnem minístrum elegísti, et per maris undas mirabíliter traduxísti: concéde; ut ejus intercessióne dignos pœniténtiæ fructus fácere, et ad ætérnæ salútis portum perveníre valeámus.

saints.name: Saint Rita of Cascia
saints.patron: Patron of impossible causes

saints.name: Saint Robert Bellarmine
saints.patron: Patron of catechists

collect.en: O God, Who endowed blessed Robert, Your Bishop and Doctor, with wondrous learning and virtue to repel the deceits of error and to defend the rights of the Apostolic See, grant, by his merits and intercession, that we may ever grow in love of truth and that the hearts of the erring may return to the unity of Your Church.
collect.la: Deus, qui ad errórum insídias repelléndas et apostólicæ Sedis jura propugnánda, beátum Robértum Pontíficem tuum atque Doctórem mira eruditióne et virtúte decorásti: ejus méritis et intercessióne concéde; ut nos in veritátis amóre crescámus et errántium corda ad Ecclésiæ tuæ rédeant unitátem.

saints.name: Saint Roch
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 16 August.
saints.about: A layman of Montpellier, in the south of France, who is said to have given away his inheritance and gone on pilgrimage to Italy, where he cared for victims of the plague and cured many. Later he was imprisoned, and he died in prison. Much of his story comes from later lives and cannot be checked. He became one of the saints most invoked in times of plague and epidemic.
saints.patron: Invoked in plague and epidemic
saints.cautions: Much of his story is uncertain.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/08-16.txt

saints.name: Saint Rose of Lima
saints.patron: Patron of Peru, Latin America and the Philippines

collect.en: Almighty God, Giver of all good things, Who willed that blessed Rose, imbued in early life with the dew of heavenly grace, should bloom among the Indians with the beauty of virginity and patience, grant unto us, Your servants, that, following the fragrance of her sweetness, we may be found worthy to become a sweet savor of Christ.
collect.la: Bonórum ómnium largítor, omnípotens Deus, qui beátam Rosam, cœléstis grátiæ rore prævéntam, virginitátis et patiéntiæ decóre Indis floréscere voluísti: da nobis fámulis tuis; ut, in odórem suavitátis ejus curréntes, Christi bonus odor éffici mereámur:

saints.name: Saint Scholastica
saints.patron: Patron of Benedictine nuns

collect.en: O God, Who, to show us the way of innocence, caused the soul of Your Virgin, blessed Scholastica, to fly up to heaven in the likeness of a dove, grant us, through her merits and prayers, to live innocently so that we may be found worthy to reach everlasting joys.
collect.la: Deus, qui ánimam beátæ Vírginis tuæ Scholásticæ ad ostendéndam innocéntiæ viam in colúmbæ spécie cœlum penetráre fecísti: da nobis ejus méritis et précibus ita innocénter vívere; ut ad ætérna mereámur gáudia perveníre.

saints.name: Saint Sebastian
saints.patron: Patron of soldiers, athletes and archers

saints.name: Saint Simon
saints.patron: Saint Jude is patron of desperate causes

collect.en: O God, Who have given us a way of coming to know Your name through Your blessed Apostles Simon and Jude, grant us to honor their everlasting glory by becoming more holy and to become more holy by honoring it.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos per beátos Apóstolos tuos Simónem et Judam ad agnitiónem tui nóminis veníre tribuísti: da nobis eórum glóriam sempitérnam et proficiéndo celebráre, et celebrándo profícere.

collect.en: O God, Who permits us to celebrate the anniversary of the death of Your holy Martyrs, Saints Sixtus, Felicissimus and Agapitus, grant that we may enjoy their companionship in everlasting happiness.
collect.la: Deus, qui nos concédis sane in Mártyrum tuórum Xysti Felicíssimi et Agapíti natalítia cólere: da nobis in ætérna beatitúdine de eórum societáte gaudére.

saints.name: Blessed Solanus Casey
saints.feastNote: Kept on 30 July in the Archdiocese of Detroit and by the Capuchins (not verified here). He is not in the General Calendar.
saints.about: A Capuchin friar and priest of Detroit, ordained without leave to preach formal sermons or hear confessions, who served for years as doorkeeper of his friary. Thousands came to him for counsel and prayer, and he urged them to thank God ahead of time. He was beatified in Detroit in 2017.
sources: Not opened in this pass: the Capuchin and Archdiocese of Detroit pages on his beatification (18 November 2017) should be checked before release.

saints.name: Saint Stanislaus
saints.patron: Patron of Poland

collect.en: O God, in defense of Whose honor Stanislaus, the glorious Bishop, died by the swords of wicked men, grant, we beseech You, that all who seek his help may obtain salvation as a result of his prayers.
collect.la: Deus, pro cujus honóre gloriósus Póntifex Stanisláus gládiis impiórum occúbuit: præsta, quǽsumus; ut omnes, qui ejus implórant auxílium, petitiónis suæ salutárem consequántur efféctum.

saints.name: Saint Stanislaus Kostka
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 15 August, the day of his death. In Poland and among the Jesuits he is kept on 13 November.
saints.about: A young Polish nobleman studying in Vienna who longed to become a Jesuit. He left on foot and walked to Rome, a journey of many hundreds of miles, to ask admission, and entered the Society of Jesus in October 1567. Within a year, on the night of the Assumption in 1568, he died at seventeen. He was canonized in 1726, and many novitiates have taken him as their protector.
saints.patron: Protector of novices

saints.name: Saint Stephen of Hungary
saints.patron: Patron of Hungary

collect.en: We beseech You, almighty God, that Your Church be worthy to have as her glorious defender in heaven blessed Stephen, Your Confessor, whom she had as her champion while he reigned on earth.
collect.la: Concéde, quǽsumus, Ecclésiæ tuæ, omnípotens Deus: ut beátum Stéphanum Confessórem tuum, quem regnántem in terris propagatórem hábuit, propugnatórem habére mereátur gloriósum in cœlis.

saints.name: Saint Stephen, The First Martyr
saints.patron: Patron of deacons

collect.en: Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord, so to imitate what we revere, that we may learn to love even our enemies; for we celebrate the heavenly birthday of him who knew how to pray for his very persecutors to our Lord Jesus Christ:
collect.la: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, imitári quod cólimus: ut discámus et inimícos dilígere; quia ejus natalícia celebrámus, qui novit étiam pro persecutóribus exoráre Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum Fílium tuum:

saints.name: Saint Tarcisius
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 15 August. Because that day is the Assumption, he has no place in the General Calendar.
saints.about: A Roman martyr known from a short poem by Pope Damasus I: carrying the Blessed Sacrament, he was set upon by a mob and chose to be beaten to death rather than give the holy Body to them. Damasus compares him to Saint Stephen. Later legend, made famous by Cardinal Wiseman’s novel Fabiola, pictured him as a boy acolyte. He was buried in the Catacomb of San Callisto.
saints.patron: Patron of altar servers and first communicants
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/08-15.txt

Wikipedia, “Tarcisius” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Saint Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
saints.patron: Co-patron of Europe

collect.en: Hear us, O God, our Savior, that as we rejoice in the feast of Blessed Teresa, Your Virgin, so we may be fed with the food of her heavenly teaching and be instructed in the affection of pious devotion.
collect.la: Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster: ut sicut de beátæ Terésiæ Vírginis tuæ festivitáte gaudémus; ita cæléstis ejus doctrínæ pábulo nutriámur, et piæ devotiónis erudiámur afféctu.

saints.name: Saint Thomas Aquinas
saints.patron: Patron of students, schools and universities

collect.en: O God, Who dost enlighten thy Church by the wonderful learning of thy blessed Confessor Thomas, and quickenest her through his godly labours, grant unto thy people, we humbly beseech thee, ever to apprehend by their understanding what he teacheth, and in their life faithfully to practice the same.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam beáti Thomæ Confessóris tui mira eruditióne claríficas, et sancta operatióne fecúndas: da nobis, quǽsumus; et quæ dócuit, intelléctu conspícere, et quæ egit, imitatióne complére.

collect.en: O God, for whose Church Bishop Thomas, now in glory, fell by the swords of wicked men, grant, we beseech You, that the prayers of all who implore his assistance may be effective and may lead to salvation.
collect.la: Deus, pro cujus Ecclésia gloriósus Póntifex Thomas gládiis impiórum occúbuit: præsta, quǽsumus; ut omnes, qui ejus implórant auxílium, petitiónis suæ salutárem consequántur efféctum.

saints.name: Saint Thomas More
saints.patron: Thomas More is patron of statesmen and politicians

saints.name: Saint Thomas the Apostle
saints.patron: Patron of India and of architects and builders

collect.en: O Lord, grant us, we beseech You, to glory in the feast-day of blessed Thomas, Your Apostle, that we may be helped continually by his patronage and imitate his faith with a devotion like his.
collect.la: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, beáti Apóstoli tui Thomæ sollemnitátibus gloriári: ut ejus semper et patrocíniis sublevémur; et fidem cóngrua devotióne sectémur.

saints.name: Saint Thérèse of the Child Jesus
saints.patron: Patron of the missions

collect.en: O Lord, Who said: Unless you become as little children, you shall not enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, grant us, we beseech You, so to follow the footsteps of blessed Theresa, the Virgin, in humility and simplicity of heart that we may obtain everlasting rewards.
collect.la: Dómine, qui dixísti: Nisi efficiámini sicut párvuli, non intrábitis in regnum cœlórum: da nobis, quǽsumus: ita sanctæ Teresiæ Vírginis in humilitáte et simplicitáte cordis vestígia sectári, ut præmia consequámur ætérna.

collect.en: O God, Who adorned blessed Titus, Your Confessor and Bishop, with the virtues of an apostle, grant, through his merits and intercession, that by living justly and piously in this world, we may be found worthy to enter heaven.
collect.la: Deus, qui beátum Titum Confessórem tuum atque Pontíficem apostólicis virtútibus decorásti: ejus méritis et intercessióne concéde; ut, juste et pie vivéntes in hoc sǽculo, ad cœléstem pátriam perveníre mereámur.

saints.name: Saint Turibius of Mogrovejo
saints.patron: Patron of the bishops of Latin America

saints.name: Saint Ursula
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 21 October, with her companions. Not in the General Calendar.
saints.about: The Martyrology commemorates Ursula and her companions, virgins killed at Cologne. A very old inscription there honours virgin martyrs, but their number and story are not known. The medieval legend of eleven thousand virgins massacred by the Huns rests on very little evidence. Saint Angela Merici placed her Ursulines under her name, and many schools bear it.
saints.cautions: Her story is legend, and the figure of eleven thousand is not history.

saints.name: Saint Valentine
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 14 February. His day was in the Roman Missal until 1969.
saints.about: The old Martyrology names two martyrs on this day: a priest of Rome, known for healing and teaching, who was beaten and beheaded on the Flaminian Way, and a bishop of Interamna (Terni) put to death in the same century. Little else is known of either. The custom of lovers’ letters on his day came much later and is not drawn from his life, but couples may rightly ask the prayers of a martyr who loved Christ more than life.
saints.patron: Popularly taken as patron of engaged and married couples
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/02-14.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/02-14.txt

collect.en: Grant, we beseech You, almighty God, that we who celebrate the anniversary of the death of Your holy Martyr, Valentine, may by his intercession be delivered from all evils that threaten us.
collect.la: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui beáti Valentíni Mártyris tui natalítia cólimus, a cunctis malis imminéntibus, ejus intercessióne, liberémur.

saints.name: Saint Veronica
saints.feastNote: The Acta Sanctorum placed her on 12 July. She is not in the General Calendar, and is not believed to be in the Roman Martyrology (not checked).
saints.about: By tradition, the woman who wiped the face of Jesus on the way to Calvary and found his likeness left on her veil. The Gospels do not tell the story; it comes from apocryphal writings and medieval legend, and some think her name grew from vera icon, “true image”. Her kindness is remembered at the sixth Station of the Cross, and photographers and laundry workers take her as patron.
saints.patron: Patron of photographers and laundry workers
saints.cautions: Her story is legend; the Gospels do not mention her.
sources: Wikipedia, “Saint Veronica” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

saints.name: Saint Vincent
saints.patron: Patron of winegrowers

collect.en: Give heed to our humble prayers, O Lord, that we who know we are guilty of our own sin, may be saved by the intercession of Your blessed Martyrs Vincent and Anastasius.
collect.la: Adésto, Dómine, supplicatiónibus nostris: ut, qui ex iniquitáte nostra reos nos esse cognóscimus, beatórum Mártyrum tuórum Vincéntii et Anastásii intercessióne liberémur.

saints.name: Saint Vincent de Paul
saints.patron: Patron of charitable works and societies

collect.en: O God, Who endowed St. Vincent with apostolic strength to preach the Gospel to the poor and to enhance the dignity of clerical life; grant, we beseech You, that we who honor his holy merits may also conform to the example of his virtues.
collect.la: Deus, qui, ad evangelizándum paupéribus et ecclesiástici órdinis decórem promovéndum, beátum Vincéntium apostólica virtúte roborásti: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, cujus pia mérita venerámur, virtútum quoque instruámur exémplis.

saints.name: Saint Vincent Ferrer
saints.patron: Patron of builders

collect.en: O God, Who graciously enlightened Your Church by the virtues and preaching of blessed Vincent, Your Confessor, grant that we, Your servants, may be taught by his example and delivered from all harm by his intercession.
collect.la: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam beáti Vincéntii Confessóris tui méritis et prædicatióne illustráre dignátus es: concéde nobis fámulis tuis; ut et ipsíus instruámur exémplis et ab ómnibus ejus patrocínio liberémur advérsis.

saints.name: Blessed Virgin Mary of Loreto
saints.patron: Patron of aviators and air travellers

saints.name: Saint Vitus
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 15 June, with Saints Modestus and Crescentia.
saints.about: A young martyr, honoured since the fifth century, who died in the persecution under Diocletian. The Martyrology names him with Modestus and Crescentia, who were brought from Sicily to Lucania and there overcame boiling lead and wild beasts before they were killed. The details are later legend. He is invoked against epilepsy and convulsive illness; the disorder once called Saint Vitus’ dance took its name from him, and dancers and actors claim him as patron.
saints.patron: Patron of dancers and actors, and of those with epilepsy
saints.cautions: The story of his martyrdom is legend; Modestus and Crescentia are probably fictitious.
sources: Roman Martyrology, traditional Latin text (1956 to 1962 editions), as transcribed by Divinum Officium (github.com/DivinumOfficium), horas/Latin/Martyrologium/06-15.txt
English Roman Martyrology as given by Divinum Officium, horas/English/Martyrologium/06-15.txt
Wikipedia, “Saint Vitus” (read October 2026; general encyclopedia, moderate reliability)

collect.en: Grant O Lord, we pray, that through the intercession of thy Holy Martyrs Vitus, Modestus and Crescentia, thy Church be not high-minded, but grow in that humility which is pleasing to thee, so that despising evil, she may practice whatever is good with unbounded charity

saints.name: Saint Zita
saints.feastNote: Roman Martyrology, 27 April.
saints.about: A servant girl of Lucca, in Tuscany, who worked for the same household from about the age of twelve until her death. She did her work as a service to God, gave food to the poor, and in time won the respect of the family that had once treated her harshly. The Martyrology remembers her for her virtues and miracles. Domestic workers take her as their patron.
saints.patron: Patron of domestic workers

saints.name: Saint Zélie Martin
saints.feastNote: Kept on 12 July with her husband, Saint Louis.
saints.about: A maker of the fine lace of Alençon, in Normandy, who ran her own business while raising her family. She married Louis Martin in 1858; of their nine children, five daughters lived to grow up, the youngest being Saint Thérèse of Lisieux. She died of breast cancer at forty-five. On 18 October 2015 Pope Francis canonized her with Louis, the first married couple canonized together.

saints.name: Saint Óscar Romero
saints.feastNote: Kept on 24 March, the day of his death (not verified here).
saints.about: Archbishop of San Salvador, who in years of violence spoke for the poor and called for an end to killing. He was shot dead while celebrating Mass on 24 March 1980. Pope Francis canonized him in 2018.
